## Appendix A Proof of Theorem 1

### A.1 Preliminaries: Symmetric and Asymmetric GLAMP

Our proof builds upon the symmetric GLAMP algorithm from [42]. We first present it below. Subsequently we present an asymmetric version that is useful to establish validity of our multi-environment GLAMP framework.

#### A.1.1 Symmetric GLAMP

The Symmetric GLAMP is introduced in [42, Theorem 2] as “Matrix-valued symmetric AMP iterations with non-separable non-linearities”. Here we restate and reformulate it in the same manner as we introduced multi-environment GLAMP in Section 3.

#### Definition A.1 (Symmetric GLAMP Instance).

Let $q\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ be fixed and known, and consider the asymptotic regime where $N\rightarrow\infty$ . A symmetric GLAMP instance is a quadruple $\{A,(f_{t})_{t\in\mathbb{N}},x^{0},Y\}$ , where $A\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}$ is a symmetric random design matrix, $Y\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}$ encodes information that the GLAMP iterates can use, $(f_{t})_{t\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a collection of mappings with $f_{t}:\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}\times\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}\to\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}$ , and $x^{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}$ is the initial condition for the GLAMP iterates.

We sometimes omit $x^{0}$ and $Y$ when they are clear from context.

#### Assumption A.9 (Symmetric GLAMP assumptions).

With the GLAMP instance in Definition A.1, we assume

- (a) $A=G+G^{{\top}}$ where $G\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}$ has iid Gaussian entries from $\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{2N})$ . This means $A$ is drawn from the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE) of dimension $N$ , denoted as $A\sim\mathrm{GOE}(N)$ .

- (b) $\limsup_{N}\frac{1}{N}\lVert Y\rVert_{2}^{2}<+\infty$ .

- (c) $\limsup_{N}\frac{1}{N}\lVert x^{0}\rVert_{2}^{2}<+\infty$ .

- (d) For each fixed $t\in\mathbb{N}$ , $f_{t}$ is uniformly Lipschitz in $N$ , in the sense that there exists some universal constant $L_{t}$ s.t. for any matrices $M_{1},M_{2},M_{1}^{\prime},M_{2}^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}$ ,

$$ \lVert f_{t}(M_{1},M_{2})-f_{t}(M_{1}^{\prime},M_{2}^{\prime})\rVert_{2}\leq L_{t}\lVert M_{1}-M_{1}^{\prime}\rVert_{2}+L_{t}\lVert M_{2}-M_{2}^{\prime}\rVert_{2},\ \forall\,N. $$

Moreover, $\limsup_{N}\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\lVert f_{t}(0,0)\rVert_{2}<+\infty$ .

- (e) Consider some fixed known $E\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ and a sequence of $E$ -partitions (groups) of $[N]$ : $[N]=\cup_{a\in[E]}C_{a}^{N}$ , and $\lim_{N\to\infty}\lvert C_{a}^{N}\rvert/N=c_{a}\in(0,1)$ . For any step $t\in\mathbb{N}$ , $f_{t}$ is separable among groups, in the sense that there are functions $g_{t,a}(\cdot,\cdot):\mathbb{R}^{\lvert C_{a}^{N}\rvert\times q}\times\mathbb{R}^{\lvert C_{a}^{N}\rvert\times q}\to\mathbb{R}^{\lvert C_{a}^{N}\rvert\times q}$ for each $a\in[E]$ , s.t.

$$ f_{t}(x^{t},Y)=\begin{bmatrix}g_{t,1}(x^{t}_{C_{1}^{N}},Y_{C_{1}^{N}})\\ g_{t,2}(x^{t}_{C_{2}^{N}},Y_{C_{2}^{N}})\\ \vdots\\ g_{t,E}(x^{t}_{C_{E}^{N}},Y_{C_{p}^{N}})\end{bmatrix}. $$

- (f) If we write $q^{0}=f_{0}(x^{0})$ , then $\forall\,a\in[E]$ ,

$$ \frac{1}{\lvert C_{a}^{N}\rvert}(q^{0}_{C_{a}^{N}})^{{\top}}q^{0}_{C_{a}^{N}}\to{\Sigma}_{a}^{0} $$

for some matrices $\{{\Sigma}_{a}^{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times q}:a\in[E]\}$ . Specifically,

$$ \frac{1}{N}(q^{0})^{T}q^{0}\rightarrow\sum_{a\in E}c_{a}\Sigma_{a}^{0}:=\Sigma^{0} $$

- (g) For any constant covariance matrices $\Sigma_{1},\Sigma_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times q}$ , any $s,r>0$ and any $a\in[E]$ ,

$$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{\lvert C_{a}^{N}\rvert}\mathbb{E}\left[g_{s,a}(Z_{1},Y_{C_{a}^{N}})^{{\top}}g_{r,a}(Z_{2},Y_{C_{a}^{N}})\right],\quad\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{\lvert C_{a}^{N}\rvert}\mathbb{E}\left[(q^{0}_{C_{a}^{N}})^{{\top}}g_{r,a}(Z_{2},Y_{C_{a}^{N}})\right] $$

exist, where $Z_{1},Z_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{\lvert C_{a}^{N}\rvert\times q}$ have iid row vectors from $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma_{1})$ and $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma_{2})$ respectively.

#### Definition A.2 (Symmetric GLAMP Iterates).

We define the GLAMP iterates corresponding to an instance $\{A,(f_{t})_{t\in\mathbb{N}},x^{0},Y\}$ as the sequence of matrices $x^{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}:t\in\mathbb{N}$ defined as follows:

$$ x^{t+1}=Af_{t}(x^{t})-f_{t-1}(x^{t-1})B_{t}^{{\top}},\ {B}_{t}=\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{N}\left(\sum_{j\in[N]}\frac{\partial(f_{t})_{j,\cdot}}{\partial x_{j,\cdot}}\right)(Z^{t})\right], $$

where $Z^{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}$ has its rows drawn iid from $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma^{t})$ with $\Sigma^{t}$ to be defined. The term ${B}_{t}$ is understood as the average of $N$ Jacobians. As $f_{t}:\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}\to\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}$ , $\frac{\partial(f_{t})_{j,\cdot}}{\partial x_{j,\cdot}}$ takes the $j$ -th row of $f_{t}(\cdot)$ as a vector function, and consider its Jacobian only w.r.t. the $j$ -th row of the input $x^{t}$ .

#### Definition A.3 (Symmetric GLAMP State Evolution).

Starting from $\Sigma^{0}$ in Assumption A.9(f), we define a sequence of matrices for ( $t\in\mathbb{N}$ ):

$$ \Sigma^{t+1}=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\left[f_{t}(Z^{t},Y)^{{\top}}f_{t}(Z^{t},Y)\right], $$

where $Z^{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}$ has iid row vectors drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma^{t})$ .

#### Theorem A.1 (Symmetric GLAMP convergence).

Under Assumption A.9, for any $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ and any sequence of uniformly order- $k$ pseudo-Lipschitz functions $\phi_{N}:\mathbb{R}^{|C_{a}^{N}|\times(3q)}\to\mathbb{R}$ for any $k\geq 1$ , the GLAMP iterates in Definition A.2 satisfy:

$$ \forall\,a\in[E],\ \phi_{N}([x^{0}_{C_{a}^{N}}|Y_{C_{a}^{N}}|x^{t}_{C_{a}^{N}}])=\mathbb{E}\left[\phi_{N}(x^{0}_{C_{a}^{N}}|Y_{C_{a}^{N}}|Z^{t}_{a})\right]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1), $$

where $Z^{t}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{\lvert C_{a}^{N}\rvert\times q}$ has its row vectors drawn iid from $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma^{t})$ .

Theorem A.1 is proved in [42] as their Theorem 2.

#### A.1.2 Asymmetric GLAMP

Many previous AMP works—including the seminal paper by Donoho et al. [13]—adopt an alternative but equivalent formulation based on an asymmetric random matrix $X$ , along with suitably defined auxiliary quantities. In this section, we articulate the asymmetric version of GLAMP following that tradition. This asymmetric version is also the prerequisite for the multi-environment version in Section 3.

#### Definition A.4 (Asymmetric GLAMP instance).

Let $q$ be a fixed and known positive integer, and consider the asymptotic regime where $\lim_{N\rightarrow+\infty}p/N\rightarrow\kappa\in(0,+\infty)$ . An asymmetric GLAMP instance is defined as a tuple

$$ \left\{X,(\Psi^{t})_{t\in\mathbb{N}},(\eta^{t})_{t\in\mathbb{N}},V^{0},B,W\right\}, $$

with the following components:

- • $X\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times p}$ is an asymmetric random design matrix;

- • $B\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}$ , $W\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}$ encode information accessible to the GLAMP iterates;

- • $(\Psi^{t})_{t\in\mathbb{N}}$ and $(\eta^{t})_{t\in\mathbb{N}}$ are sequences of update mappings, where

$$ \Psi^{t}:\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}\times\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}\to\mathbb{R}^{N\times q},\quad\eta^{t}:\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\times\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\to\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}; $$

- • $V^{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}$ is the initial condition for the GLAMP iterates.

As in prior formulations, the components $V^{0}$ , $B$ , and $W$ are omitted from notation when the context is clear. The following assumptions are associated with the asymmetric GLAMP instance:

#### Assumption A.10 (Asymmetric GLAMP assumptions).

Given the GLAMP instance in Definition A.4, we make the following assumptions:

- (a) The matrix $X\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times p}$ has i.i.d. entries drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,1/N)$ .

- (b) The matrices $B\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}$ and $W\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}$ satisfy

$$ \limsup_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\|B\|_{2}<\infty,\quad\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\|W\|_{2}<\infty. $$

- (c) The initial condition $V^{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}$ satisfies

$$ \limsup_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\|V^{0}\|_{2}^{2}<\infty. $$

- (d) For each fixed $t\in\mathbb{N}$ , the mappings $\Psi^{t}$ are uniformly Lipschitz in $N$ , and $\eta^{t}$ are uniformly Lipschitz in $p$ . In addition,

$$ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\|\Psi^{t}(0,0)\|_{2}<\infty,\quad\limsup_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\|\eta^{t}(0,0)\|_{2}<\infty. $$

- (e) Fix $E\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ , and let $[N]=\bigcup_{a\in[E]}C_{a}^{N}$ be a sequence of partitions (groups) such that $\lim_{N\to\infty}|C_{a}^{N}|/N=c_{a}\in(0,1)$ . For any $t\in\mathbb{N}$ , the function $\Psi^{t}$ is separable across groups, i.e., there exist mappings

$$ \Psi_{a}^{t}:\mathbb{R}^{|C_{a}^{N}|\times q}\times\mathbb{R}^{|C_{a}^{N}|\times q}\to\mathbb{R}^{|C_{a}^{N}|\times q} $$

such that

$$ \Psi^{t}(R^{t},W)=\begin{bmatrix}\Psi_{1}^{t}(R^{t}_{C_{1}^{N}},W_{C_{1}^{N}})\\ \Psi_{2}^{t}(R^{t}_{C_{2}^{N}},W_{C_{2}^{N}})\\ \vdots\\ \Psi_{E}^{t}(R^{t}_{C_{E}^{N}},W_{C_{E}^{N}})\end{bmatrix}. $$

- (f) The initial condition satisfies

$$ \frac{1}{p}\left(\eta^{0}(V^{0})\right)^{\top}\eta^{0}(V^{0})\to\Sigma_{(R)}^{0} $$

for some matrix $\Sigma_{(R)}^{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times q}$ .

- (g) For any fixed covariance matrices $\Sigma_{1},\Sigma_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times q}$ , and any $s,r\geq 0$ , $a\in[E]$ , the following limit exists:

$$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{|C_{a}^{N}|}\mathbb{E}\left[\Psi_{a}^{s}(Z_{1},W_{C_{a}^{N}})^{\top}\Psi_{a}^{r}(Z_{2},W_{C_{a}^{N}})\right], $$

where $Z_{1},Z_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{|C_{a}^{N}|\times q}$ have i.i.d. rows drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma_{1})$ and $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma_{2})$ , respectively.

- (h) For any fixed covariance matrices $\Sigma_{1},\Sigma_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times q}$ , and any $s,r\geq 1$ , the following limits exist:

$$ \lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\eta^{s}(Z_{1},B)^{\top}\eta^{r}(Z_{2},B)\right],\quad\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\eta^{0}(V^{0},B)^{\top}\eta^{r}(Z_{2},B)\right], $$

where $Z_{1},Z_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}$ have i.i.d. rows drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma_{1})$ and $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma_{2})$ , respectively.

Given an instance, the asymmetric GLAMP iterates and their corresponding state evolution are defined as follows:

#### Definition A.5 (Asymmetric GLAMP iterates).

Let $\{X,(\Psi^{t})_{t\in\mathbb{N}},(\eta^{t})_{t\in\mathbb{N}},V^{0},B,W\}$ be an asymmetric GLAMP instance satisfying Assumption A.10. The asymmetric GLAMP iterates are the alternating sequence of matrices $\{(V^{t},R^{t}):t\in\mathbb{N}\}$ , initialized with

$$ R^{0}=X\eta^{0}(V^{0},B). $$

For $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ , the iterates are defined recursively as:

$$ \displaystyle V^{t} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{\kappa}X^{\top}\Psi^{t-1}(R^{t-1},W)-\frac{1}{\kappa}\eta^{t-1}(V^{t-1},B)\left[D_{(R)}^{t-1}\right]^{\top},\quad \displaystyle D_{(R)}^{t-1} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{j\in[N]}\left(\frac{\partial(\Psi^{t-1})_{j,\cdot}}{\partial(R^{t-1})_{j,\cdot}}\right)(Z_{(R)}^{t-1})\right], \displaystyle R^{t} \displaystyle=X\eta^{t}(V^{t},B)-\Psi^{t-1}(R^{t-1},W)\left[D_{(V)}^{t}\right]^{\top},\quad \displaystyle D_{(V)}^{t} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{j\in[p]}\left(\frac{\partial(\eta^{t})_{j,\cdot}}{\partial(V^{t})_{j,\cdot}}\right)(Z_{(V)}^{t})\right], $$

where the Gaussian random matrices $Z_{(R)}^{t-1}$ and $Z_{(V)}^{t}$ will be defined in the state evolution equations (Definition A.6).

#### Definition A.6 (Asymmetric GLAMP state evolutions).

Starting from the initialization $\Sigma^{0}_{(R)}$ as given in Assumption A.10 (f), we define a sequence of matrices as follows:

For $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ ,

$$ \Sigma^{t}_{(V)}=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\left[\Psi^{t-1}(Z^{t-1}_{(R)},W)^{\top}\Psi^{t-1}(Z^{t-1}_{(R)},W)\right], $$

where $Z^{t-1}_{(R)}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}$ has i.i.d. rows drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,\kappa\,\Sigma^{t-1}_{(R)})$ .

Next,

$$ \Sigma^{t}_{(R)}=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\eta^{t}(Z^{t}_{(V)},B)^{\top}\eta^{t}(Z^{t}_{(V)},B)\right], $$

where $Z^{t}_{(V)}\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}$ has i.i.d. rows drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{\kappa^{2}}\Sigma^{t}_{(V)})$ .

#### Corollary A.1 (Asymmetric GLAMP convergence).

Let $t\in\mathbb{N}$ . Consider the iterates defined in Definition A.4 under Assumption A.10. Then:

- • For any order- $k$ pseudo-Lipschitz function $\phi:(\mathbb{R}^{p\times q})^{3}\to\mathbb{R}$ , with $k\geq 1$ , we have

$$ \phi(V^{t},V^{0},B)=\mathbb{E}\left[\phi(Z^{t}_{(V)},V^{0},B)\right]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1), $$

where $Z^{t}_{(V)}\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}$ has i.i.d. rows sampled from $\mathcal{N}(0,\kappa^{-2}\Sigma^{t}_{(V)})$ , as defined in Definition A.6.

- • For any $a\in[E]$ and any order- $k$ pseudo-Lipschitz function $\phi:(\mathbb{R}^{|C_{a}^{N}|\times q})^{2}\to\mathbb{R}$ , with $k\geq 1$ , we have

$$ \phi(R^{t}_{C_{a}^{N}},W_{C_{a}^{N}})=\mathbb{E}\left[\phi(Z^{t}_{(R)},W_{C_{a}^{N}})\right]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1), $$

where $Z^{t}_{(R)}\in\mathbb{R}^{|C_{a}^{N}|\times q}$ has i.i.d. rows drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,\kappa\Sigma^{t}_{(R)})$ , also defined in Definition A.6.

Corollary A.1 is a direct consequence of Theorem A.1, and its proof is omitted.

### A.2 Proof of Theorem 1

#### Proof of Theorem 1.

We start from Corollary A.1, together with its full set of assumptions, and specify it down to the form of the multi-environment GLAMP. Then we relax some of the assumptions to get Theorem 1.

Suppose we have $E$ environments, each with a sample size $n_{e}$ , $N=\sum_{e\in[E]}n_{e}$ . We define $\kappa_{e}=\lim_{p}\frac{p}{n_{e}}$ , and $\delta_{e}=\sqrt{n_{e}/N}$ . We partition the large Gaussian matrix $X\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times p}$ , $X_{i,j}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{iid}}}{{\sim}}\mathcal{N}(0,1/N)$ into $X=[\delta_{1}X_{1}|\delta_{2}X_{2}|\cdots|\delta_{E}X_{E}]^{{\top}}$ , where $X_{e}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{e}\times p}$ and $X_{i,j}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{iid}}}{{\sim}}\mathcal{N}(0,1/n_{e})$ . Specifically each of $Z^{t}_{(V,e)}\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q_{0}}$ has iid rows from $\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{\kappa_{e}^{2}}\Sigma_{(V,e)}^{t})$ ,

For the matrices involved in the Onsager terms, we get after some algebra: ( $Z^{t}_{(V)}=[Z^{t}_{(V,1)}|Z^{t}_{(V,2)}|\cdots|Z^{t}_{(V,E)}]$ )

$$ \displaystyle D^{t-1}_{(R)}= \displaystyle\diag\left(\left\{\frac{\delta_{e}}{N}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{j\in[n_{e}]}\left(\frac{\partial(\Psi^{t-1}_{e})_{j,\cdot}}{\partial(R^{t-1}_{e})_{j,\cdot}}\right)(Z_{(R,e)}^{t-1})\right]:e\in[E]\right\}\right), \displaystyle D^{t}_{(V)}= \displaystyle\left[\frac{1}{p\delta_{e_{2}}}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{j\in[p]}\frac{\partial(\eta^{t}_{e_{2}})_{j}}{\partial(V_{e_{1}}^{t})_{j}}\left(Z^{t}_{(V)},B\right)\right]\right]_{e_{1}\in[E],e_{2}\in[E]}. $$

Now we have all the ingredients to write out the multi-environment GLAMP:

$$ \displaystyle V_{e}^{t}= \displaystyle\frac{1}{\kappa_{e}}X_{e}^{{\top}}\Psi^{t-1}_{e}(R_{e}^{t-1},W_{e})-\frac{1}{\kappa_{e}}\eta^{t-1}_{e}(V_{1}^{t-1},\cdots,V_{E}^{t-1},B)[D^{t-1}_{(R,e)}]^{{\top}}, \displaystyle D_{(R,e)}^{t-1}=\frac{1}{n_{e}}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{j\in[n_{e}]}\left(\frac{\partial(\Psi_{e}^{t-1})_{j,\cdot}}{\partial(R_{e}^{t-1})_{j,\cdot}}\right)(Z_{(R,e)}^{t-1})\right], \displaystyle R_{e}^{t}= \displaystyle X_{e}\eta_{e}^{t}(V_{1}^{t},V_{2}^{t},\cdots,V_{E}^{t},B)-\Psi^{t-1}_{e}(R_{e}^{t-1},W_{e})[D_{(V,e)}^{t}]^{{\top}}, \displaystyle D_{(V,e)}^{t}=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{j\in[p]}\left(\frac{\partial(\eta_{e}^{t})_{j,\cdot}}{\partial(V^{t}_{e})_{j,\cdot}}\right)(Z_{(V)}^{t})\right]. $$

Under Assumption 1 with all the specification made, we already have convergence results taking the form of those from Theorem 1. However, Assumption A.9 is stronger than Assumption 1, because the former would have required the following limits to exist

$$ \lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\eta_{e_{1}}^{s}(Z_{1},B)^{{\top}}\eta_{e_{2}}^{r}(Z_{2},B)\right],\quad\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(\eta_{e_{1}}^{0}({V^{0},B}))^{{\top}}\eta_{e_{2}}^{r}(Z_{2},B)\right] $$

for any $e_{1},e_{2}\in[E]$ , any constant covariance matrices $\Sigma_{1},\Sigma_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times q}$ and any $s,r\geq 1$ . In contrast, Assumption 1 only requires the same limits to exist for $e=e_{1}=e_{2}$ . In other words, we need to relax the assumptions we are working under.

Instead of going to the proof details of GLAMP, we use a sub-sequence argument to prove the convergence results under Assumption 1. To show

$$ \displaystyle\left\lvert\phi(V_{1}^{t},V_{2}^{t},\cdots,V_{E}^{t},V^{0},B)-\mathbb{E}\left[\phi(Z_{(V,1)}^{t},Z_{(V,2)}^{t},\cdots,Z_{(V,E)}^{t},V^{0},B)\right]\right\rvert\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathbb{P}}}{{\to}}0 $$

under Assumption 1, we take any sub-sequence $(p^{\prime},n_{1}^{\prime},\cdots,n_{E}^{\prime})$ of $(p,n_{1},n_{2},\cdots,n_{E})$ and show it admits a further subsequence that makes the above convergence hold almost surely, with the GLAMP iterates and covariance matrices $\{\Sigma^{t}_{(V,e)}:e\in[E],t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}\}$ involved independent of the choice of the sub-sequences.

Firstly, for any fixed $t$ , there are only finitely many covariance matrices involved in the state evolution. By Assumption 1, we know there exists a further sub-sequence $(p^{\prime\prime},n_{1}^{\prime\prime},\cdots,n_{E}^{\prime\prime})$ such that the limits

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}(\eta^{0}(V^{0}))^{{\top}}\eta^{0}(V^{0})\to{\Sigma}^{0}_{(R)},\ a.s., \displaystyle\Sigma^{s}_{(V)}=\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\left[\Psi^{s-1}(Z_{(R)}^{s-1},W)^{{\top}}\Psi^{s-1}(Z_{(R)}^{s-1},W)\right], \displaystyle\Sigma^{s}_{(R)}=\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\eta^{s}(Z_{(V)}^{s},B)^{{\top}}\eta^{s}(Z_{(V)}^{s},B)\right] $$

exists for $1\leq s\leq t$ under the specification in Equation (A-3), (A-4) along the sub-sequence $(p^{\prime\prime},n_{1}^{\prime\prime},\cdots,n_{E}^{\prime\prime})$ . The $E$ diagonal blocks of the shapes $q_{e}\times q_{e}$ from ${\Sigma}^{0}_{(R)},\Sigma^{s}_{(V)},\Sigma^{s}_{(R)}$ are guaranteed by Assumption 1 to exist independently of the sub-sequence $(p^{\prime},n_{1}^{\prime},\cdots,n_{e}^{\prime})$ , but the off-diagonal blocks can depend on $(p^{\prime\prime},n_{1}^{\prime\prime},\cdots,n_{e}^{\prime\prime})$ .

Secondly, along the sub-sequence $(p^{\prime\prime},n_{1}^{\prime\prime},\cdots,n_{e}^{\prime\prime})$ , there exists a further sub-sequence $(p^{\prime\prime\prime},n_{1}^{\prime\prime\prime},\cdots,n_{e}^{\prime\prime\prime})$ s.t. all the following limits exist along $(p^{\prime\prime\prime},n_{1}^{\prime\prime\prime},\cdots,n_{e}^{\prime\prime\prime})$

$$ \lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\eta_{e_{1}}^{s}(Z_{(V)}^{s},B)^{{\top}}\eta_{e_{2}}^{r}(Z_{(V)}^{r},B)\right],\quad\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(\eta_{e_{1}}^{0}({V^{0},B}))^{{\top}}\eta_{e_{2}}^{r}(Z^{r}_{(V)},B)\right] $$

for all $e_{1}\neq e_{2}$ , $1\leq s\leq r\leq t$ , and for all $Z_{(V)}^{s}$ with iid rows drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma^{s}_{(V)})$ , $Z_{(V)}^{r}$ with iid rows drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma^{r}_{(V)})$ . Along $(p^{\prime\prime\prime},n_{1}^{\prime\prime\prime},\cdots,n_{e}^{\prime\prime\prime})$ , we can invoke Corollary A.1 to get

$$ \displaystyle\left\lvert\phi(V_{1}^{t},V_{2}^{t},\cdots,V_{E}^{t},V^{0},B)-\mathbb{E}\left[\phi(Z_{(V,1)}^{t},Z_{(V,2)}^{t},\cdots,Z_{(V,E)}^{t},V^{0},B)\right]\right\rvert\to 0 $$

in probability along $(p^{\prime\prime\prime},n_{1}^{\prime\prime\prime},\cdots,n_{e}^{\prime\prime\prime})$ , and almost surely along a further sub-sequence of $(p^{\prime\prime\prime},n_{1}^{\prime\prime\prime},\cdots,n_{e}^{\prime\prime\prime})$ .

Lastly, we note that (i) the multi-environment GLAMP iterates in Equation (1) do not change its definition with any special sub-sequence of $(p,n_{1},\cdots,n_{E})$ , and (ii) the state evolution enough to characterize their behavior in Definition 4 is fully determined by Assumption 1, independently of the choice of sub-sequences. In other words, whichever sub-sequence we are working on, the covariance matrices $\Sigma^{t}_{(V,1)},\Sigma^{t}_{(V,2)},\cdots,\Sigma^{t}_{(V,E)}$ used to characterize $Z^{t}_{(V,1)},Z^{t}_{(V,2)},\cdots,Z^{t}_{(V,E)}$ stay the same.

As a result, we have shown under Assumption 1,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lvert\phi(V_{1}^{t},V_{2}^{t},\cdots,V_{E}^{t},V^{0},B)-\mathbb{E}\left[\phi(Z_{(V,1)}^{t},Z_{(V,2)}^{t},\cdots,Z_{(E,2)}^{t},V^{0},B)\right]\right\rvert\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathbb{P}}}{{\to}}0. $$

The same argument applies to $\left\lvert\phi(R^{t}_{e},W_{e})-\mathbb{E}\left[\phi(Z^{t}_{e},W_{e})\right]\right\rvert\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathbb{P}}}{{\to}}0$ . This completes the proof of Theorem 1. ∎

## Appendix B Proofs of Auxiliary Results in Section 4

### B.1 Proof of Proposition 1

We first show all the alternative forms of $\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{e}$ are equivalent. Then we show the limit $\lim_{p}\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{e}=\overline{\delta}_{e}$ is well-defined.

By the extended Stein’s Lemma in our Lemma F.3, we immediately have $\frac{1}{\tau_{e}p}\mathbb{E}\left[Z_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\overline{\eta}(\tau_{1},\tau_{2},\cdots,\tau_{E})\right]=\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{\partial(\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\overline{\eta})_{j}}{\partial(\tau_{e}Z_{e})_{j}}\right]$ , which is the first equality of Equation (6). The second equality in Equation (6) is due to a rewriting of the summed partial derivatives. Then we prove the third line of Equation (6). Recall that $\overline{\eta}(\tau_{1},\tau_{2},\cdots,\tau_{E})=\eta(\tau_{1}Z_{1},\tau_{2}Z_{2},\cdots,\tau_{E}Z_{E})$ , where the function $\eta$ is defined in Equation (3). Denote the support of $\overline{\eta}$ by $S$ . By $\eta$ ’s definition and the KKT condition of the ‘argmin’ part, we know $\overline{\eta}_{S}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ satisfies

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{e\in[E]}\varpi_{e}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S}\overline{\eta}_{S}-\sum_{e\in[E]}\varpi_{e}(\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})_{S,\cdot}(\tau_{e}Z_{e})-\sum_{e\in[E]}\varpi_{e}(\Sigma_{e}\beta_{e})_{S}+\theta\diag({\vec{\lambda}})\mathop{\mathrm{sign}}(\overline{\eta}_{S})=0, $$

while the KKT conditions for $\overline{\eta}_{S^{c}}$ are slack ones. By the implicit function theorem,

$$ \frac{\partial\overline{\eta}_{S}}{\partial(\tau_{e}Z_{e})}=\bigg[\sum_{e\in[E]}\varpi_{e}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S}\bigg]^{-1}\varpi_{e}(\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})_{S,\cdot}. $$

Thus from the second line of Equation (6), we know

$$ \overline{\delta}_{e}^{{(p)}}=\varpi_{e}\cdot\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\bigg(\bigg[\sum_{e\in[E]}\varpi_{e}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S}\bigg]^{-1}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S}\bigg)\right], $$

thus proving the third line of Equation (6).

We are left to prove $\lim_{p}\overline{\delta}_{e}^{(p)}=\overline{\delta}_{e}$ . We know from Assumption 3(c) that

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\partial\mathcal{E}^{{(p)}}}{\partial\tau_{e}}=-\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\varpi_{e}Z_{e}^{{\top}}\left[\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\overline{\eta}-(\tau_{e}Z_{e}+\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e})\right]\right]=-\frac{1}{p}\varpi_{e}\mathbb{E}\left[Z_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\overline{\eta}\right]+\varpi_{e}\tau_{e} $$

converges to some limit as $p\to\infty$ . Thus $\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[Z_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\overline{\eta}]$ has a well-defined limit, proving $\overline{\delta}_{e}=\lim_{p}\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{e}$ .

By the third line of Equation (6), $\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}^{(p)}=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\lvert S\rvert]=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\lVert\overline{\eta}\rVert_{0}]$ . As $p\to\infty$ , we know $\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\lVert\overline{\eta}\rVert_{0}]=\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}$ . This completes the proof of Proposition 1.

### B.2 Proof of Proposition 3

We first study the equivalent forms of $\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}^{(p)}$ and then $\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}^{(p)}$ . For $\overline{\gamma}^{(p)}_{\textup{II}}$ , we invoke Stein’s lemma (our Lemma F.3) to get

$$ \overline{\gamma}^{(p)}_{\textup{II}}=\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{\partial(\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\xi)_{j}}{\partial(v_{\textup{II}})_{j}}(\tau_{\textup{II}}Z_{\textup{II}},\overline{\eta})\right]=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left(\frac{\partial\overline{\xi}}{\partial v_{\textup{II}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\right)\right]=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left(\frac{\partial(\overline{\xi}-\overline{\eta})}{\partial v_{\textup{II}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\right)\right]. $$

In the case of $\mu_{\textup{II}}=\mu_{\mathrm{joint}}$ , we have the KKT condition of $\overline{\xi}$ on the support of $S_{\textup{II}}=\mathrm{supp}(\overline{\xi}-\overline{\eta})$ in Equation (B-7):

$$ (\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}(\overline{\xi}-\overline{\eta})_{S_{\textup{II}}}-(\Sigma^{1/2}_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},\cdot}(\tau_{\textup{II}}Z_{\textup{II}})-(1-\kappa_{1}\gamma_{\textup{I}})(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},\cdot}(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta})+\theta_{\textup{II}}\lambda_{\textup{II}}\mathop{\mathrm{sign}}(\overline{\xi}-\overline{\eta})_{S_{\textup{II}}}=0. $$

$$ \frac{\partial(\overline{\xi}-\overline{\eta})_{S_{\textup{II}}}}{\partial v_{\textup{II}}}=\left[(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}\right]^{-1}(\Sigma^{1/2}_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},\cdot}\implies\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}^{(p)}=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left(\left[(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}\right]^{-1}(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}\right)\right]=\frac{\mathbb{E}[\lvert S_{\textup{II}}\rvert]}{p}. $$

In the case of $\mu_{\textup{II}}=\mu_{\mathrm{ada}}$ , we have the KKT condition of $\xi$ on the support $S_{\textup{II}}=\mathrm{supp}(\overline{\xi})$ in Equation (B-9), where $D_{\mu}$ has shown up in Equation (19) as a diagonal matrix, $(D_{\mu})_{j}=\mu(\lvert(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})_{j}\rvert)$ .

$$ (\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}\overline{\xi}_{S_{\textup{II}}}-(\Sigma^{1/2}_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},\cdot}(\tau_{\textup{II}}Z_{\textup{II}})-(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},\cdot}\beta_{1}+\kappa_{1}\gamma_{\textup{I}}(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},\cdot}(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta})+\theta_{\textup{II}}(D_{\mu})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}\mathop{\mathrm{sign}}(\overline{\xi})_{S_{\textup{II}}}=0. $$

So we similarly have

$$ \frac{\partial\overline{\xi}_{S_{\textup{II}}}}{\partial v_{\textup{II}}}=\left[(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}\right]^{-1}(\Sigma^{1/2}_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},\cdot}\implies\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}^{(p)}=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left(\left[(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}\right]^{-1}(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}\right)\right]=\frac{\mathbb{E}[\lvert S_{\textup{II}}\rvert]}{p}. $$

After studying $\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}$ , we look at $\overline{\gamma}^{(p)}_{\textup{I}}$ , We first invoke Stein’s lemma and the chain rule of derivatives to get

$$ \displaystyle\overline{\gamma}^{(p)}_{\textup{I}}= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{\partial(\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\xi)_{j}}{\partial\hat{\beta}}(\tau_{\textup{II}}Z_{\textup{II}},\overline{\eta})\right)^{{\top}}\frac{\partial\overline{\eta}}{\partial(\tau_{1}^{*}Z_{1})_{j}}\right]=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left(\frac{\partial\xi}{\partial\hat{\beta}}(\tau_{\textup{II}}Z_{\textup{II}},\overline{\eta})\frac{\partial\overline{\eta}}{\partial(\tau_{1}^{*}Z_{1})}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\right)\right]. $$

In the case of $\mu_{\textup{II}}=\mu_{\mathrm{joint}}$ , we know

$$ \frac{\partial\xi}{\partial\hat{\beta}}(\tau_{\textup{II}}Z_{\textup{II}},\overline{\eta})\frac{\partial\overline{\eta}}{\partial(\tau_{1}^{*}Z_{1})}=\frac{\partial(\overline{\xi}-\overline{\eta})}{\partial\hat{\beta}}(\tau_{\textup{II}}Z_{\textup{II}},\overline{\eta})\frac{\partial\overline{\eta}}{\partial(\tau_{1}^{*}Z_{1})}+\frac{\partial\overline{\eta}}{\partial(\tau_{1}^{*}Z_{1})}, $$

and

$$ \frac{\partial(\overline{\xi}-\overline{\eta})_{S_{\textup{II}}}}{\partial\overline{\eta}}=-(1-\kappa_{1}\gamma_{\textup{I}})\left[(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}\right]^{-1}(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},\cdot}. $$

Combined with Equation (B-5), we know (with $S=\mathrm{supp}(\overline{\eta})$ , $\overline{\Sigma}=\sum_{e}\varpi_{e}^{*}\Sigma_{e}$ from Section B.1)

$$ \displaystyle\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}^{(p)}= \displaystyle\overline{\delta}_{1}^{(p)}-\varpi_{1}^{*}(1-\kappa_{1}\gamma_{\textup{I}})\cdot\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left(\left[(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}\right]^{-1}(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S}\left[\overline{\Sigma}_{S,S}\right]^{-1}(\Sigma_{1})_{S,S_{\textup{II}}}\right)\right]. $$

In the case of $\mu_{\textup{II}}=\mu_{\mathrm{ada}}$ , we similarly have

$$ \frac{\partial\overline{\xi}_{S_{\textup{II}}}}{\partial\overline{\eta}}=\kappa_{1}\gamma_{\textup{I}}\left[(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}\right]^{-1}(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},\cdot} $$

and

$$ \displaystyle\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}^{(p)}= \displaystyle\varpi_{1}^{*}\kappa_{1}\gamma_{\textup{I}}\cdot\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left(\left[(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}\right]^{-1}(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S}\left[\overline{\Sigma}_{S,S}\right]^{-1}(\Sigma_{1})_{S,S_{\textup{II}}}\right)\right]. $$

Now we have studied the equivalent forms of $\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}^{(p)}$ , $\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}^{(p)}$ . We then move on to prove the existence of the limits. First off, we show the limit $\lim_{p}\overline{\gamma}^{(p)}_{\textup{I}}=\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}$ . We look at $({\partial\mathcal{E}^{(p)}_{\textup{II}}})/({\partial\zeta})$ which admits a limit by Assumption 7 (b). After some algebra,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{{\partial\mathcal{E}^{(p)}_{\textup{II}}}}{{\partial\zeta}}= \displaystyle-\frac{\tau_{\textup{II}}}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(Z_{1}-\zeta Z_{1}^{\prime}/\sqrt{1-\zeta^{2}}\right)^{{\top}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\overline{\xi}\right]+\tau_{\textup{II}}\,\kappa_{1}\,\gamma_{\textup{I}}\,\tau_{1}^{*}\,\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{1}=\tau_{\textup{II}}\tau_{1}^{*}\left(\kappa_{1}\,\overline{\delta}^{{(p)}}_{1}\gamma_{\textup{I}}-\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}^{(p)}\right). $$

By Assumption 7 (b), we know there exists some $\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}$ such that $\lim_{p}\overline{\gamma}^{(p)}_{\textup{I}}=\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}$ . Next we show there exists some value $\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}\geq 0$ , s.t. $\lim_{p}\overline{\gamma}^{(p)}_{\textup{II}}=\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}$ , which is implied by

$$ \displaystyle\frac{{\partial\mathcal{E}^{(p)}_{\textup{II}}}}{{\partial\tau_{\textup{II}}}}= \displaystyle\tau_{\textup{II}}(1-\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}^{(p)})+\zeta\cdot\tau_{E}^{*}(\kappa_{E}\overline{\delta}_{E}^{(p)}\gamma_{\textup{I}}-\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}^{(p)}) $$

and Assumption 7 (a).

$$ \displaystyle v_{e}^{t}= \displaystyle{\displaystyle X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}(y_{e}-r_{e}^{t-1})-\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}+\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\eta(v_{1}^{t-1},v_{2}^{t-1},\cdots,v_{E}^{t-1}), \displaystyle r_{e}^{t}= \displaystyle{\displaystyle X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\eta(v_{1}^{t},v_{2}^{t},\cdots,v_{E}^{t})-\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{e}(y_{e}-r_{e}^{t-1}) $$

for all $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ and $e\in[E]$ . #### Definition C.2 (State Evolution).

Let $\Sigma_{(V,e)}\in(\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_{+}})\times(\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_{+}})$ be infinite-dimensional matrices defined as below: $\forall\,e\in[E]$ ,

For all $i\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ , $(\Sigma_{(V,e)})_{i,i}=(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}$ .

For all $i<j$ , $i,j\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ , $(\Sigma_{(V,e)})_{i,j}=(\Sigma_{(V,e)})_{j,i}=(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}\rho_{e}^{i,j}$ , where $\rho_{e}^{i,j}\in[0,1]$ , $\rho^{i,j}=(\rho^{i,j}_{1},\rho^{i,j}_{2},\cdots,\rho^{i,j}_{E})\in[0,1]^{E}$ . #### Lemma C.2 (GLAMP Convergence).

Under Assumptions 2,3,4, and Definitions C.1,C.2, $\forall\,t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ , $\forall\,$ sequence of order- $k$ pseudo-Lipschitz functions $\phi:(\mathbb{R}^{p})^{(t+1)E+1}\to\mathbb{R}$ , $k\geq 1$ ,

#### Lemma C.3 (The Cauchy Property).

Under Assumptions 2,3,4, and Definitions C.1,C.2, $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , $\exists\,T=T(\epsilon)$ . s.t. $\forall\,j>i\geq T$ , $\forall e\in[E]$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert v_{e}^{j}-v_{e}^{i}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\epsilon\right]=1,\quad \displaystyle\lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[\frac{1}{n_{e}}\left\lVert r_{e}^{j}-r_{e}^{i}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\epsilon\right]=1, \displaystyle\lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\bigg[\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert\eta^{j}-\eta^{i}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\epsilon\bigg]=1,\quad \displaystyle\max_{e\in[E]}\{1-\rho_{e}^{i,j}\}\leq\epsilon. $$

Under Assumptions 2,3,4, and Definitions C.1,C.2, define a vector $s^{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ by

#### Proof of Theorem 2.

We work with small $\epsilon$ and $t\geq T$ required by Lemma C.6. By Lemma C.1 and Lemma C.2, we have $\lim_{p}\mathbb{P}\left[\max\{\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2},\frac{1}{p}\lVert\eta^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}\}\leq M\right]=1$ . By Assumption 2(c), we can choose $M$ large enough s.t. $\limsup_{p}\frac{1}{p}\lVert\beta_{e}\rVert_{2}^{2}<M\ \forall\,e\in[E]$ as well. So we can choose $\epsilon$ small enough s.t. with probability approaching $1$ as $p\to\infty$ at a fixed $t$ , for any sequence of order- $k$ pseudo-Lipschitz functions $\phi:(\mathbb{R}^{p})^{E+1}\to\mathbb{R}$ $(k\geq 1)$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lvert\phi(\eta^{t},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})-\phi(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})\right\rvert \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle L\left[1+\sum_{e\in[E]}\left(\frac{\lVert\beta_{e}\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}}\right)^{k-1}+\left(\frac{\lVert\eta^{t}\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}}\right)^{k-1}+\left(\frac{\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}}\right)^{k-1}\right]\frac{\lVert\eta^{t}-\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}}\leq\frac{\epsilon}{2}. $$

Also with probability going to 1 as $p\to\infty$ , we have $\lvert\phi(\eta^{t},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})-\mathbb{E}\left[\phi(\overline{\eta},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})\right]\rvert<\epsilon/2$ by Lemma C.2. Thus for any small enough $\epsilon$ , we have $\lvert\phi(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})-\mathbb{E}\left[\phi(\overline{\eta},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})\right]\rvert<\epsilon$ with probability going to 1 as $p\to\infty$ . This proves Theorem 2. ∎

### C.1 Proof of Auxiliary Lemmas in Section C

#### C.1.1 Proof of Lemma C.1

The proof follows the same steps as those of Lemma 3.2, Bayati and Montanari [32]. First of all,

$$ \displaystyle\limsup_{p}L(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})/p\leq\limsup_{p}L(0)/p\leq\sum_{e\in[E]}\pi_{e}\cdot\frac{\lVert y_{e}\rVert_{2}^{2}}{2p}\leq\sum_{e\in[E]}\pi_{e}\cdot\left[\frac{\lVert w_{e}\rVert_{2}^{2}}{p}+\frac{\sigma_{\max}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}})^{2}c_{1}^{2}\lVert\beta_{e}\rVert_{2}^{2}}{p}\right]. $$

By Lemma F.4, $\lim_{p}\sigma_{\max}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}})=1+\sqrt{\kappa_{e}},a.s.$ . By Assumption 2, we know $\limsup_{p}L(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})/p<+\infty$ . Now if $\kappa_{e}<1$ for any $e:\pi_{e}>0$ , then we know $\liminf_{p}\sigma_{\min}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})\geq(1-\sqrt{\kappa_{e}})/c_{1}^{1/2}>0$ by Lemma F.4 and Assumption 2, and thus $\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq B_{1}\cdot\frac{1}{p}\lVert{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\ a.s.$ for some constant $B_{1}>c_{1}/(1-\sqrt{\kappa_{e}})^{2}$ as $p\to\infty$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\frac{2}{p}\left[\lVert y_{e}-{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}+\lVert y_{e}\rVert_{2}^{2}\right]\leq\frac{2}{\pi_{e}}\left[\frac{L(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})}{p}+\frac{L(0)}{p}\right], $$

and we have proved Lemma C.1. From now on, we focus on the the case of $\kappa_{e}\geq 1$ for all the environments $e:\pi_{e}>0$ .

For any $e:\pi_{e}>0$ , let $P_{e}^{\|}$ be the projection matrix onto $\mathrm{\ker}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})$ and $P_{e}^{\bot}$ onto $\mathrm{\ker}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})^{\bot}$ . Then $\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\frac{1}{p}\lVert P_{e}^{\|}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}+\frac{1}{p}\lVert P_{e}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}$ . At any finite $p$ , $\mathrm{\ker}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})$ is still a uniformly random space, so Kashin’s theorem (c.f. Lemma F.5) applies just like in the proof of Lemma 3.2, Bayati and Montanari [32]. For some constant $B_{1}$ , the relationship below holds almost surely as $p\to\infty$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq B_{1}\left(\frac{1}{p}\lVert P_{e}^{\|}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{1}\right)^{2}+\frac{1}{p}\lVert P_{e}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 2B_{1}\left(\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{1}\right)^{2}+\frac{2B_{1}+1}{p}\lVert P_{e}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}. $$

The first inequality in the above line uses Kashin’s theorem, and the second has omitted some details because they are the same as those in Bayati and Montanari [32]. For the former term, $\limsup_{p}\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{1}<+\infty,a.s.$ because $\limsup_{p}\frac{1}{p}L(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})<+\infty$ . For the latter term, since $\mathrm{\ker}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})^{\bot}=\mathrm{range}(\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}})$ , $P_{e}^{\bot}=\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}})^{-1}{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}$ . By Lemma F.4 and Assumption 2, there exists $B_{2}>0$ s.t.

$$ \lVert P_{e}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}\leq B_{2}\lVert{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}P_{e}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}=B_{2}\lVert{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2},a.s., $$

and $\lVert{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}$ has been bounded by Equation (C-15). Now we have shown $\limsup_{p}\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}<+\infty$ .

#### C.1.2 Proof of Lemma C.2

#### Proof of Lemma C.2.

The way to prove Lemma C.2 is to show the GLAMP instance defined in Definition C.1 is a legitimate multi-environment GLAMP as defined in Definition 2. However, we are faced with one more technicality: we have used external randomness to initialize the iterates. As a result, the original GLAMP would give results conditioning on a realization of $\eta^{0}$ , which is not exactly Lemma C.2.

We use a sub-sequence argument to address this technicality. We know from Lemma F.2 and Assumption 3 that, ( $\overline{\eta}=\overline{\eta}(\tau_{1}^{*},\tau_{2}^{*},\cdots,\tau_{E}^{*})$ )

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\eta^{0}= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}\right]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1) \displaystyle\implies\mathop{\mathrm{plim}}_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\eta^{0}=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}\right], \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}(\eta^{0})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\eta^{0}= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}\right]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1) \displaystyle\implies\mathop{\mathrm{plim}}_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}(\eta^{0})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\eta^{0}=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}\right], \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}(\eta^{0})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\mathbb{E}[\overline{\eta}]= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}_{(1)}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{(2)}\right]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1) \displaystyle\implies\mathop{\mathrm{plim}}_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}(\eta^{0})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\mathbb{E}[\overline{\eta}]=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}_{(1)}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{(2)}\right], $$

where in the last line, $\overline{\eta}_{(1)}$ and $\overline{\eta}_{(2)}$ are mutually independent copies of $\overline{\eta}$ . The existence of the limit $\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}_{(1)}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{(2)}\right]$ is implied by $\lim_{p}H^{{(p)}}=H$ in Assumption 4(b) combined with Assumption 3(b).

Recall that a sequence of random variables converges in probability iff any of its sub-sequences admit a further sub-sequence that converges almost surely. If we prove Lemma C.2 along any sub-sequence of $(p,n_{1},n_{2},\cdots,n_{E})$ on which the three limits involving $\eta^{0}$ in Equation (C-16) all hold almost surely (instead of merely in probability), we will have proved Lemma C.2 itself. This is because any sub-sequence of $(p,n_{1},n_{2},\cdots,n_{E})$ firstly admits a further sub-sequence along which all the limits in Equation (C-16) hold almost surely. If we prove the desired convergence in Lemma C.2 along the further sub-sequence, we will have proved Lemma C.2 itself, since the limit is free of the choice of specific sub-sequences.

With a slight abuse of notation, we still use letters $(p,n_{1},n_{2},\cdots,n_{E})$ to denote the sub-sequence along with the three limits involving $\eta^{0}$ in Equation (C-16) all hold almost surely.

$$ \displaystyle\ V_{e}^{t}= \displaystyle\left[v_{e}^{1}|v_{e}^{2}|\cdots|v_{e}^{t}|0|0|\cdots\right], \displaystyle\eta_{e}^{t}(V_{1}^{t},\cdots,V_{E}^{t})= \displaystyle\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\left[\beta_{e}|\eta^{0}|\eta(v_{1}^{1},\cdots,v_{E}^{1})|\eta(v_{1}^{2},\cdots,v_{E}^{2})|\cdots|\eta(v_{1}^{t},\cdots,v_{E}^{t})|0|0|\cdots\right], \displaystyle R_{e}^{t}= \displaystyle\left[{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}|r_{e}^{0}|r_{e}^{1}|\cdots|r_{e}^{t}|0|0|\cdots\right], \displaystyle\Psi_{e}^{t}(R_{e}^{t})= \displaystyle\kappa_{e}\left[y_{e}-r_{e}^{0}|y_{e}-r_{e}^{1}|\cdots|y_{e}-r_{e}^{t}|0|0|\cdots\right]\quad(y_{e}={X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}+w_{e}). $$

where the Gaussian variables used are yet to be characterized by the state evolution.

To fully write out its form, we need the state evolution first. From there, we prove the whole state evolution for $V^{t}_{e}$ with induction.

#### C.1.3 Proof of Lemma C.3

We first prove a lemma and then use it to prove Lemma C.3.

#### Lemma C.7.

For the function $H$ defined in Assumption 4(b) and any $e\in[E]$ , its $e$ -th element $H_{e}=H_{e}(\rho_{1},\cdots,\rho_{E})$ is increasing and strictly convex in $\rho_{i}$ , $\forall\,i\in[E]$ , while we fix $\{\rho_{j}:j\neq i\}$ . We have

$$ 0\leq\frac{\partial H_{e}}{\partial\rho_{i}}\leq\frac{\kappa_{e}(\tau_{i}^{*})^{2}\varpi_{i}^{*}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}\varpi^{*}_{e}}\overline{\delta}_{i}\overline{\delta}_{e}. $$

The first half of Proposition C.7 follows the same argument as that of Lemma C.1 of Bayati and Montanari [32], or Lemma C.2 of Donoho and Montanari [33]. To elaborate, we first assume without loss of generality that $i=1$ . We represent the function $H_{e}$ in an alternative way. Let $H_{e}=\lim_{p}H^{{(p)}}_{e}$ , where $H^{{(p)}}_{e}$ is the finite- $p$ version of the same function, i.e.

$$ \displaystyle H_{e}^{{(p)}}(\rho_{1},\rho_{2},\cdots,\rho_{E})= \displaystyle\frac{1}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}\left\{\mathbb{E}[W_{e}^{2}]+\kappa_{e}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(\overline{\eta}_{{(1)}}-\beta_{e})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}(\overline{\eta}_{{(2)}}-\beta_{e})\right]\right\} \displaystyle\mathrm{where}\ \overline{\eta}_{{(1)}}= \displaystyle\eta(\tau^{*}_{1}\sqrt{\rho_{1}}Z_{1}+\tau_{1}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{1}}Y_{1},\tau^{*}_{2}\sqrt{\rho_{2}}Z_{2}+\tau_{2}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{2}}Y_{2},\cdots,\tau^{*}_{E}\sqrt{\rho_{E}}Z_{E}+\tau_{E}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{E}}Y_{E}), \displaystyle\overline{\eta}_{{(2)}}= \displaystyle\eta(\tau^{*}_{1}\sqrt{\rho_{1}}Z_{1}+\tau_{1}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{1}}Y_{1}^{\prime},\tau^{*}_{2}\sqrt{\rho_{2}}Z_{2}+\tau_{2}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{2}}Y_{2}^{\prime},\cdots,\tau^{*}_{E}\sqrt{\rho_{E}}Z_{E}+\tau_{E}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{E}}Y_{E}^{\prime}), $$

and $\{Z_{e}\}$ , $\{Y_{e}\}$ , $\{Y_{e}^{\prime}\}$ are a total of $(3E)$ iid $\mathcal{N}(0,I_{p})$ variables. Then $H_{e}$ can be further rewritten with a function $\nu:\mathbb{R}^{p}\to\mathbb{R}^{p}$ as follows:

$$ \displaystyle H_{e}= \displaystyle\frac{\mathbb{E}[W_{e}^{2}]}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}+\frac{\kappa_{e}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[\nu(\sqrt{\rho_{1}}Z_{1}+\sqrt{1-\rho_{1}}Y_{1})^{{\top}}\nu(\sqrt{\rho_{1}}Z_{1}+\sqrt{1-\rho_{1}}Y_{1}^{\prime})\middle|Z_{2},Z_{3},\cdots,Z_{E}\right]\right], \displaystyle\nu(\cdot)= \displaystyle\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\left\{\mathbb{E}\left[\eta(\tau_{1}^{*}(\,\cdot\,),\tau^{*}_{2}\sqrt{\rho_{2}}Z_{2}+\tau_{2}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{2}}Y_{2},\cdots,\tau^{*}_{E}\sqrt{\rho_{E}}Z_{E}+\tau_{E}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{E}}Y_{E})\middle|Z_{2},Z_{3},\cdots,Z_{E}\right]\right\}. $$

We introduce a total of $p$ iid stationary Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes with covariance function $\exp\left(-t\right)$ , stacked as a vector $X_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ , then $H_{e}^{(p)}=\frac{\mathbb{E}[W_{e}^{2}]}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}+\frac{\kappa_{e}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[\nu(X_{0})^{{\top}}\nu(X_{t})\middle|Z_{2},Z_{3},\cdots,Z_{E}\right]\right]$ , $t=\log(1/\rho_{1})$ . With the same eigen-decomposition trick as that of Lemma C.1 of Bayati and Montanari [32], or Lemma C.2 of Donoho and Montanari [33], we can show $H_{e}^{{(p)}}$ is increasing and strictly convex in $\rho_{1}\in[0,1]$ , and thus so is $H_{e}$ . We have proved the first half of Proposition C.7.

To show $0\leq\frac{\partial H_{e}}{\partial\rho_{i}}\leq\frac{\kappa_{e}(\tau_{i}^{*})^{2}\varpi_{i}^{*}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}\varpi^{*}_{e}}\overline{\delta}_{i}\overline{\delta}_{e}$ , we only need to show $0\leq\frac{\partial H_{e}}{\partial\rho_{i}}(\vec{1}_{E})\leq\frac{\kappa_{e}(\tau_{i}^{*})^{2}\varpi_{i}^{*}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}\varpi^{*}_{e}}\overline{\delta}_{i}\overline{\delta}_{e}$ , where $\vec{1}_{E}$ is a vector of all ones in $R^{E}$ . Without loss of generality, still assume $i=1$ .

We first compute the partial derivatives at a general $\rho=(\rho_{1},\cdots,\rho_{E})$ , and then set $\rho=\vec{1}_{E}$ . Suppose the limit can be exchanged with the partial derivative, we have

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\partial H_{e}}{\partial\rho_{1}}= \displaystyle\frac{\kappa_{e}\tau_{1}^{*}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(\overline{\eta}_{(2)}-\beta_{e})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}J_{1}(\overline{\eta}_{(1)})\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\rho_{1}}}Z_{1}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\rho_{1}}}Y_{1}\right)\right], $$

where we have used the exchangeability of $Y_{1}$ and $Y_{1}^{\prime}$ to simplify the form. The notation ‘ $J_{1}(\overline{\eta}_{(1)})$ ’ means the $p$ -by- $p$ Jacobian matrix of $\overline{\eta}_{(1)}$ w.r.t. $(\tau_{1}^{*}\sqrt{\rho_{1}}Z_{1}+\tau_{1}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{1}}Y_{1})$ . $$ \displaystyle\frac{\partial H_{e}}{\partial\rho_{1}}= \displaystyle\frac{\kappa_{e}\tau_{1}^{*}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(\overline{\eta}_{(2)}-\beta_{e})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}J_{1}(\overline{\eta}_{(1)})\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\rho_{1}}}Z_{1}\right)\right]=\frac{\kappa_{e}(\tau_{1}^{*})^{2}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left(J_{1}(\overline{\eta}_{(2)})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}J_{1}(\overline{\eta}_{(1)})\right)\right]. $$

In the inequality above, we have used a trace inequality that $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(AB)\leq\lambda_{\max}(A)\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(B)\leq\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(A)\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(B)$ for $A,B$ both positive semi-definite [80, see e.g. Theorem 1 of]. So far we have proved Proposition C.7. ∎

#### Proof of Lemma C.3.

We start by studying $\mathop{\mathrm{plim}}_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert v_{e}^{t+1}-v_{e}^{t}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}$ . Using Lemma C.2, we know $\mathop{\mathrm{plim}}_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert v_{e}^{t+1}-v_{e}^{t}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}=2(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}(1-\rho_{e}^{t,t+1})$ . We plan to show $\rho_{e}^{t,t+1}$ converges exponentially fast to 1 for each $e\in[E]$ with an argument of fixed point iteration.

By the multi-variate mean-value theorem, for any $\rho_{(1)}\in[0,1]^{E}$ and $\rho_{(2)}=H(\rho_{(1)})$ , there exists some point $\rho_{\mathrm{tmp}}$ , which is a convex combination of $\rho_{(1)},\rho_{(2)}$ , s.t. $\vec{1}_{E}-\rho_{(2)}=H(\vec{1}_{E})-H(\rho_{(1)})=J(H(\rho_{\mathrm{tmp}}))(\vec{1}_{E}-\rho_{(1)})$ . $J(H(\rho_{\mathrm{tmp}}))\in\mathbb{R}^{E\times E}$ is the Jacobian matrix. $$ \displaystyle 0\leq(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}\varpi_{e}^{*}(1-\rho_{(2),e})\leq\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}\sum_{i\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{i}(\tau_{i}^{*})^{2}\varpi_{i}^{*}(1-\rho_{(1),i})\leq\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}\max_{e\in[E]}\{\overline{\delta}_{e}\}\sum_{i\in[E]}(\tau_{i}^{*})^{2}\varpi_{i}^{*}(1-\rho_{(1),i}) \displaystyle\implies 0\leq\sum_{e\in[E]}(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}\varpi_{e}^{*}(1-\rho_{(2),e})\leq\max_{e\in[E]}\left\{\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}\right\}\max_{e\in[E]}\left\{\overline{\delta}_{e}\right\}\sum_{e\in[E]}(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}\varpi_{e}^{*}(1-\rho_{(1),e}). $$

By Assumption 4(a), we know $\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}<1$ ; by Proposition 1, we know $\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\lVert\overline{\eta}\rVert_{0}]\leq 1$ . As a result, $\max_{e\in[E]}\left\{\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}\right\}\max_{e\in[E]}\left\{\overline{\delta}_{e}\right\}<1$ . By a fixed-point iteration argument, we know $\rho_{e}^{t,t+1}$ converges exponentially fast to 1. As a result, $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , there exists $T$ s.t. $\forall\,j>i\geq T$ , $\max_{e\in[E]}\left\{1-\rho_{e}^{i,j}\right\}<\epsilon$ .

The rest of Lemma C.3 is easily implied by what we have proved. Hence the Cauchy property of $\{r^{t}_{e}\}$ also follows.
