We need to prepare some definitions, and Lemma C.8, C.9 to prove Lemma C.5.

For any constant $c\in(0,1)$ , define $S^{t}(c)=\{j\in[p]:\lvert s^{t}_{j}\rvert\geq 1-c\}$ where $s^{t}$ has been defined in Equation (C-14). We also define the ‘idealized’ versions of them indicated by overlines:

$$ \overline{s}\in\mathbb{R}^{p},\ \overline{s}=\frac{1}{\theta^{*}}\left[\diag(\vec{\lambda})^{-1}\right]\sum_{e\in[E]}\varpi_{e}^{*}(\tau_{e}^{*}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}Z_{e}+\Sigma_{e}(\beta_{e}-\eta(\tau_{1}^{*}Z_{1},\cdots,\tau_{E}^{*}Z_{E}))), $$

where $Z_{1},Z_{2},\cdots,Z_{E}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{iid}}}{{\sim}}\mathcal{N}(0,I_{p})$ . We still use $\overline{\eta}=\eta(\tau_{1}^{*}Z_{1},\cdots,\tau_{E}^{*}Z_{E})$ as a shorthand, but note that we will be using the same $Z_{1},Z_{2},\cdots,Z_{E}$ throughout the proof. We define $\overline{S}(c)=\{j\in[p]:\lvert\overline{s}_{j}\rvert\geq 1-c\}$ . We also define a set of re-scaled quantities indicated with tildes: Let $\lambda_{\min,\mathrm{all}}=\min_{e\in[E]}\{\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{e})\}$ . We define $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{e}=\Sigma_{e}/\lambda_{\min,\mathrm{all}}$ , $\widetilde{\tau}^{*}_{e}=\tau_{e}^{*}/\sqrt{\lambda_{\min,\mathrm{all}}}$ , $\widetilde{\theta}^{*}=\theta^{*}/{\lambda_{\min,\mathrm{all}}}$ . We also define one covariance without subscript, $\widetilde{\Sigma}=\sum_{e\in[E]}\varpi_{e}^{*}\widetilde{\Sigma}_{e}$ .

Define a new quantity $\tilde{\eta}^{t}=\eta^{t}+\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\diag(\vec{\lambda})s^{t}$ and its idealized counterpart $\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ , $\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}=\overline{\eta}+\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\diag(\vec{\lambda})\overline{s}$ . About $\tilde{\eta}^{t}$ and $\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}$ , we notice $S^{t}(c)=\{j\in[p]:\lvert\tilde{\eta}^{t}_{j}\rvert\geq\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}(1-c)\}$ , $\overline{S}(c)=\{j\in[p]:\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}^{t}_{j}\rvert\geq\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}(1-c)\}$ . This is because $s^{t}$ and $\overline{s}$ are respectively the sub-gradients of $\lVert\eta^{t}\rVert_{1}$ and $\lVert\overline{\eta}\rVert_{1}$ .

Define $\widetilde{Z}=\sum_{e\in[E]}\varpi_{e}^{*}\widetilde{\tau}^{*}_{e}(\widetilde{\Sigma})^{-1/2}\widetilde{\Sigma}_{e}^{1/2}Z_{e}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ , then $\widetilde{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sum_{e\in[E]}(\varpi_{e}^{*}\widetilde{\tau}_{e}^{*})^{2}\widetilde{\Sigma}^{-1/2}\widetilde{\Sigma}_{e}\widetilde{\Sigma}^{-1/2})$ . For the covariance matrix of $\widetilde{Z}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\liminf_{p}\lambda_{\min}\bigg(\sum_{e\in[E]}(\varpi_{e}^{*}\widetilde{\tau}_{e}^{*})^{2}\widetilde{\Sigma}^{-1/2}\widetilde{\Sigma}_{e}\widetilde{\Sigma}^{-1/2}\bigg)\geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{c_{1}^{2}}{\sum_{e\in[E]}(\varpi_{e}^{*}\widetilde{\tau}_{e}^{*})^{2}}>0. $$

We note that $\overline{\eta}$ depend on $(Z_{1},Z_{2},\cdots,Z_{E})$ only through $\widetilde{Z}$ . Moreover, $\widetilde{\Sigma}^{1/2}\overline{\eta}$ is 1-Lipschitz w.r.t. $\widetilde{Z}$ . To see why these hold true, we rewrite $\overline{\eta}$ as below and invoke the Lipschitz property of proximal operators.

$$ \displaystyle\overline{\eta}= \displaystyle\argmin_{b}\bigg\{\sum_{e\in[E]}\frac{1}{2}\varpi_{e}^{*}\left\lVert\widetilde{\Sigma}_{e}^{1/2}b-\widetilde{\tau}_{e}^{*}Z_{e}-\widetilde{\Sigma}_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}+\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\left\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda})b\right\rVert_{1}\bigg\} \displaystyle= \displaystyle\argmin_{\beta}\bigg\{\frac{1}{2}\lVert\widetilde{\Sigma}^{1/2}b\rVert_{2}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2(\widetilde{\Sigma}^{1/2}b)^{{\top}}\widetilde{Z}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\sum_{e\in[E]}b^{\top}\widetilde{\Sigma}\beta_{e}+\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\left\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda})b\right\rVert_{1}\bigg\}. $$

We also express $\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}$ in terms of $\widetilde{Z}$ . we get

$$ \displaystyle\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}= \displaystyle\sum_{e\in[E]}\varpi_{e}^{*}\widetilde{\Sigma}_{e}\beta_{e}+\widetilde{\Sigma}^{1/2}\left[\widetilde{Z}-(I_{p}-\widetilde{\Sigma}^{-1})\widetilde{\Sigma}^{1/2}\overline{\eta}\right]. $$

For each $j\in[p]$ , define $\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ as the $j$ -th row vector of $\widetilde{\Sigma}^{1/2}$ (written vertically despite being a row vector). We note that $\lVert\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}\rVert_{2}\geq 1$ . This is because $1\leq\lambda_{\min}(\widetilde{\Sigma}^{1/2})=\inf_{\lVert u\rVert_{2}=1}\lVert\widetilde{\Sigma}^{1/2}u\rVert_{2}\leq\lVert P_{-j}^{\bot}\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}\rVert_{2}\leq\lVert\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}\rVert_{2}$ where $P^{\bot}_{-j}\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times p}$ is the projection matrix onto the orthogonal complement of $\Span(\widetilde{\sigma}_{i}:i\neq j)$ , and $u$ could be taken as $u=P^{\bot}_{-j}\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}/\lVert P^{\bot}_{-j}\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}\rVert_{2}$ .

Let $\widetilde{Z}_{j}=\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}^{{\top}}\widetilde{Z}\in\mathbb{R}$ . We know from Equation (C-18) and $\lVert\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}\rVert_{2}\geq 1$ that $\liminf_{p}\mathop{\mathrm{var}}(\widetilde{Z}_{j})\geq\sum_{e}(\varpi_{e}^{*}\widetilde{\tau}_{e}^{*})^{2}/c_{1}^{2}>0$ .

We try to write $\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}$ as a function of $\widetilde{Z}_{j}$ and study that function. Define $P_{j}^{\bot}$ as the projection matrix onto the orthogonal complement of $\Span(\widetilde{\sigma}_{j})$ . Notice that $\widetilde{Z}=\frac{\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}^{{\top}}\widetilde{Z}}{\lVert\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}\rVert_{2}^{2}}\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}+P^{\bot}_{j}\widetilde{Z}=\frac{\widetilde{Z}_{j}}{\lVert\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}\rVert_{2}^{2}}\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}+P^{\bot}_{j}\widetilde{Z}$ , where $\widetilde{Z}_{j}\mathchoice{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\displaystyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\displaystyle\perp}}}{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\textstyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\textstyle\perp}}}{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\scriptstyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\scriptstyle\perp}}}{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\scriptscriptstyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle\perp}}}P^{\bot}_{j}\widetilde{Z}$ . We define $f_{j}(\widetilde{Z}_{j})=(I-\widetilde{\Sigma}^{-1})\widetilde{\Sigma}^{1/2}\overline{\eta}$ . Then $f_{j}(\widetilde{Z}_{j})$ is a function of $\widetilde{Z}_{j}$ but also determined by $P^{\bot}_{j}\widetilde{Z}$ as well as $\{Z_{e^{\prime}}:e^{\prime}\neq e\}$ , but these Gaussian variables are all independent from $\widetilde{Z}_{j}$ . Conditioning on them, $\widetilde{\Sigma}^{1/2}\overline{\eta}$ is $\lVert\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}\rVert_{2}^{-1}$ -Lipschitz in $\widetilde{Z}_{j}$ . Notice by the construction of $\widetilde{\Sigma}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde{\Sigma}^{-1})= \displaystyle\lambda_{\min}(\widetilde{\Sigma})^{-1}\leq\min_{e}\{\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{e})\}/[\sum_{e}\varpi_{e}^{*}\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{e})]\leq 1, \displaystyle\lambda_{\min}(\widetilde{\Sigma}^{-1})= \displaystyle\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde{\Sigma})^{-1}\geq\min_{e}\{\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{e})\}/\max_{e}\left\{\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma_{e})\right\}. $$

We define the ratio $\kappa_{cond}^{-1}=\min_{e}\{\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{e})\}/\max_{e}\{\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma_{e})\}$ . Then $f_{j}(\cdot)$ is $(1-\kappa_{cond}^{-1})\lVert\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}\rVert_{2}^{-1}$ -Lipschitz.

We then look at how $\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}$ is related to $\widetilde{Z}_{j}$ , and write $\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}=h_{j}(\widetilde{Z}_{j})$ . By the form of $\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}$ in Equation (C-19), we know $h_{j}$ is also determined jointly by $\widetilde{Z}_{j}$ and $P^{\bot}_{j}\widetilde{Z}$ , $\{Z_{e^{\prime}}:e^{\prime}\neq e\}$ . Given any $P^{\bot}_{j}\widetilde{Z}$ and $\{Z_{e^{\prime}}:e^{\prime}\neq e\}$ , the function $h_{j}(\cdot)$ is Lipschitz continuous, and satisfies

$$ \displaystyle\lvert h_{j}(x_{1})-h_{j}(x_{2})\rvert\geq \displaystyle\lvert x_{1}-x_{2}\rvert-\lvert\widetilde{\sigma}_{j}^{{\top}}\left(f_{j}(x_{1})-f_{j}(x_{2})\right)\rvert\geq\kappa^{-1}_{cond}\lvert x_{1}-x_{2}\rvert. $$

With Equation (C-20) prepared, we need a few more lemmas:

#### Lemma C.8.

Let $\{I_{a}\subset\mathbb{R}:a>0\}$ be a collection of intervals indexed by $a>0$ , satisfying $\lim_{a\downarrow 0}m(I_{a})=0$ where $m(\cdot)$ is the Lebesgue measure. Then $\lim_{a\downarrow 0}\sup_{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbf{1}{\{\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\in I_{a}\}}\right]=0$ .

#### Proof of Lemma C.8.

$\mathbb{P}[\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\in I_{a}]=\mathbb{P}[h(\widetilde{Z}_{j})\in I_{a}]=\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{P}[h(\widetilde{Z}_{j})\in I_{a}|P_{j}^{\bot}\widetilde{Z},\{Z_{e^{\prime}}:e^{\prime}\neq e\}]\right]$ . For any fixed $P_{j}^{\bot}\widetilde{Z}$ and $\{Z_{e^{\prime}}:e^{\prime}\neq e\}$ , Equation (C-20) implies there exists an interval ${I}$ , s.t. $m({I})\leq\kappa_{cond}\,m(I_{a})$ and $\{h(\widetilde{Z}_{j})\in I_{a}\}|_{P_{j}^{\bot}\widetilde{Z},\{Z_{e^{\prime}}:e^{\prime}\neq e\}}=\{\widetilde{Z}_{j}\in I\}$ . This is because otherwise there must be $x_{1}\neq x_{2}$ s.t. $h_{j}(x_{1})=h_{j}(x_{2})$ but $\lvert x_{1}-x_{2}\rvert>0$ , contradicting Equation (C-20). As a result,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{P}[h(\widetilde{Z}_{j})\in I_{a}|P_{j}^{\bot}\widetilde{Z},\{Z_{e^{\prime}}:e^{\prime}\neq e\}]\right]\leq\sup_{I:m(I)\leq\kappa_{cond}m(I_{a})}\mathbb{P}\left[\widetilde{Z}_{j}\in I\right]\leq\frac{\kappa_{cond}\,m(I_{a})}{\sqrt{2\pi(\sum_{e}(\varpi_{e}^{*}\widetilde{\tau}_{e}^{*})^{2}/c_{1}^{2})}}, $$

where the second inequality has simply used the upper bound on the density of a normal distribution. Lemma C.8 follows right from the above line. ∎

#### Lemma C.9.

For any fixed $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ and $c\in(0,1)$ , $\lvert S^{t}(c)\rvert/p=\mathbb{E}[\lvert\overline{S}(c)\rvert/p]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1)$ .

#### Proof of Lemma C.9.

We fix $c$ for the rest of the proof. We define the notation $(x)_{+}=\max\{x,0\},\forall\,x\in\mathbb{R}$ . For $0<a<\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)/3$ , define a Lipschitz function $\phi^{(1)}_{1}(x):\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ : $\phi^{(1)}_{1}(x)=[1-(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)-\lvert x\rvert)_{+}/a]_{+}$ . Then $\lvert\phi^{(1)}_{1}(x)-\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert x\rvert\geq\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)\}}\rvert\leq\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert x\rvert\in(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)-a,\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c))\}}$ .

For any $x\in\mathbb{R}$ , define $\mathrm{dist}(x)$ as the distance of $\lvert x\rvert$ to the interval $(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)-a,\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c))$ , i.e. $\mathrm{dist}(x)=(\lvert x\rvert-\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c))_{+}+(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)-a-\lvert x\rvert)_{+}$ . Define another Lipschitz function $\phi^{(1)}_{2}(x):\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ : $\phi^{(1)}_{2}(x)=(1-\mathrm{dist}(x)/a)_{+}$ . Then $\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert x\rvert\in(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)-a,\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c))\}}\leq\phi^{(1)}_{2}(x)\leq\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert x\rvert\in(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)-2a,\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)+a)\}}$ . For $i=1,2$ , define $\phi_{i}^{{(p)}}:\mathbb{R}^{p}\to\mathbb{R}$ : $\forall\,x\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ , $\phi_{i}^{{(p)}}(x)=\sum_{j\in[p]}\phi^{(1)}_{i}(x_{j})$ . By Lemma F.1, both $\{\phi_{1}^{{(p)}}:p\geq 1\}$ and $\{\phi_{2}^{{(p)}}:p\geq 1\}$ are uniformly Lipschitz functions.

It is already known that $S^{t}(c)=\{j\in[p]:\lvert\tilde{\eta}^{t}_{j}\rvert\geq\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}(1-c)\}$ , $\widetilde{S}(c)=\{j\in[p]:\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}^{t}_{j}\rvert\geq\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}(1-c)\}$ . By Lemma C.2, for any already chosen and fixed $a$ , as $p\to\infty$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lvert{\lvert S^{t}(c)\rvert}/{p}-\mathbb{E}[{\lvert\overline{S}(c)\rvert}/{p}]\right\rvert\leq \displaystyle\lvert\phi_{1}^{(p)}(\tilde{\eta}^{t})-\mathbb{E}[\phi_{1}^{(p)}(\overline{\widetilde{\eta}})]\rvert+\phi_{2}^{(p)}(\tilde{\eta}^{t})+\mathbb{E}[\phi_{2}^{(p)}(\overline{\widetilde{\eta}})]\leq 2\mathbb{E}[\phi_{2}^{(p)}(\overline{\widetilde{\eta}})]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1) \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{2}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\rvert\in(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)-2a,\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)+a)\}}]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1). $$

By Lemma C.8, for any $\epsilon>0$ , we can fix a small $a$ s.t. $\sup_{p}\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\rvert\in(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)-2a,\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)+a)\}}]<\epsilon/4$ before taking $p\to\infty$ . Thus Lemma C.9 is proved. ∎

#### Proof of Lemma C.5.

For any chosen and fixed $c\in(0,1)$ , we know from Lemma C.9, $\lvert S^{t}(c)\rvert/p=\mathbb{E}[\lvert\overline{S}(c)\rvert/p]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1)$ as $p\to\infty$ . Furthermore,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\lvert\overline{S}(c)\rvert/p]= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\rvert>\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}\}}\right]+\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\rvert\in(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}(1-c),\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}]\}}\right]. $$

Lemma C.8 implies $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , $\exists\,c\in(0,1)$ small enough s.t. $\sup_{p}\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\rvert\in(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}(1-c),\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j})\}}]<\epsilon$ . By the definition of $\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\rvert>\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}\}}\right]= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\lVert\overline{\eta}\rVert_{0}\right]=\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}^{(p)}\to\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}, $$

where the second equality is by Equation (B-6) and the convergence is by Proposition 1.

By the choice of $c$ so far, we know it only depends on the ‘idealized’ quantities such as $\overline{\eta}$ and $\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}$ , not any specific time step $t$ . As a result, $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , there exists $c=c(\epsilon)\in(0,1)$ s.t. fixing any $c^{\prime}\in(0,c]$ and any $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ , we have $\lim_{p}\mathbb{P}\left[\lvert S^{t}(c^{\prime})\rvert/p\leq\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon\right]=1$ . This completes the proof. ∎

#### C.1.6 Proof of Lemma C.6

We need to introduce Lemma C.10 as preparation for the proof of Lemma C.6.

First off, we assume without loss of generality that $\pi_{e}>0$ for all $e\in[E]$ ; that is, all the environments $(y_{e},{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})$ that have contributed to $\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}$ have been assigned positive weights in the loss function in Equation (2). This does not lose generality because by Assumption 2 and 4(a), $\pi_{e}=0$ iff $\varpi_{e}^{*}=0$ ; in other words, when one environment is assigned no weight in the loss function in Equation (2), it does not enter the GLAMP formulation either, so we can just ignore it.

Secondly, let $N=\sum_{e\in[E]}n_{e}$ , $\kappa=\lim_{p}p/N=(\sum_{e\in[E]}\kappa_{E}^{-1})^{-1}$ , and define

$$ y_{\mathrm{stack}}=\begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{\pi_{1}}y_{1}\\
\sqrt{\pi_{2}}y_{2}\\
\vdots\\
\sqrt{\pi_{E}}y_{E}\end{bmatrix},X_{\mathrm{stack}}=\begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{\pi_{1}}{X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\\
\sqrt{\pi_{2}}{X_{2}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{2}^{1/2}\\
\vdots\\
\sqrt{\pi_{E}}{X_{E}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{E}^{1/2}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{\frac{n_{1}}{N}}{X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{1}N}{n_{1}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\\
\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}}{N}}{X_{2}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{2}N}{n_{2}}}\Sigma_{2}^{1/2}\\
\vdots\\
\sqrt{\frac{n_{E}}{N}}{X_{E}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{E}N}{n_{E}}}\Sigma_{E}^{1/2}.\end{bmatrix} $$

Now we can rewrite the loss function in Equation (2) as $L(b)=\frac{1}{2}\lVert y_{\mathrm{stack}}-X_{\mathrm{stack}}b\rVert_{2}^{2}+\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda})b\rVert_{1}$ .

Lastly, define the sparse singular eigenvalues of a matrix. For any matrix $X$ having $p$ columns, any subset $S\subset[p]$ , define $\kappa_{-}(X,S)=\inf\left\{\lVert Xu\rVert_{2}:\mathrm{supp}(u)\subset S,\lVert u\rVert_{2}=1\right\}$ and the $k$ -sparse singular value

$$ \kappa_{-}(X,k)=\min_{S\subset[p],\lvert S\rvert\leq k}\kappa_{-}(X,S). $$

Of course $\kappa_{-}(X,k)$ is decreasing in $k$ for fixed $X$ ; when $k\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ , the definition in Equation (C-22) can be equivalently written as $\kappa_{-}(X,k)=\min_{S\subset[p],\lvert S\rvert=k}\kappa_{-}(X,S)$ .

#### Lemma C.10 (Lower Bound on the Sparse Singular Values).

Under Assumption 2 and the definition in Equation (C-21), there exists small enough constants $\epsilon_{0}>0$ and $c_{0}>0$ , s.t. $\kappa\cdot(\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon_{0})<1$ , and $\forall\,\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_{0})$ ,

$$ \lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[\kappa_{-}\left(X_{\mathrm{stack}},p(\textstyle\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon)\right)>c_{0}\right]=1. $$

#### Proof of Lemma C.10.

We use $X_{\mathrm{temp}}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times p}$ to denote a matrix of iid $\mathcal{N}(0,1/N)$ elements, and divide it into blocks as $(X_{\mathrm{temp}})^{{\top}}=\left[(X_{\mathrm{temp},1})^{{\top}}|(X_{\mathrm{temp},2})^{{\top}}|\cdots|(X_{\mathrm{temp},E})^{{\top}}\right]$ , where $X_{\mathrm{temp},e}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{e}\times p}$ . For $X_{\mathrm{stack}}$ in Equation (C-21), and any index set $S\subset[p]$ , the following equality in distribution holds:

$$ (X_{\mathrm{stack}})_{\cdot,S}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{d}}}{{=}}\begin{bmatrix}(X_{\mathrm{temp},1})_{\cdot,S}\left({\frac{\pi_{1}N}{n_{1}}}(\Sigma_{1})_{S,S}\right)^{1/2}\\
(X_{\mathrm{temp},2})_{\cdot,S}\left({\frac{\pi_{2}N}{n_{2}}}(\Sigma_{2})_{S,S}\right)^{1/2}\\
\vdots\\
(X_{\mathrm{temp},E})_{\cdot,S}\left({\frac{\pi_{E}N}{n_{E}}}(\Sigma_{E})_{S,S}\right)^{1/2}.\end{bmatrix} $$

To see why the equality in distribution holds, note that each block of $(X_{\mathrm{stack}})_{\cdot,S}$ satisfies $[\sqrt{\frac{n_{e}}{N}}{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}]_{\cdot,S}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{d}}}{{=}}[X_{\mathrm{temp},e}(\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}}\Sigma_{e})^{1/2}]_{\cdot,S}=X_{\mathrm{temp},e}[(\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}}\Sigma_{e})^{1/2}]_{\cdot,S}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times\lvert S\rvert}$ . Each row of $X_{\mathrm{temp},e}[(\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}}\Sigma_{e})^{1/2}]_{\cdot,S}$ is an iid draw from $\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S})$ , so the block is equal in distribution to $(X_{\mathrm{temp},e})_{\cdot,S}({\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S})^{1/2}$ .

Since $\liminf_{p\to\infty}\min_{e\in[E]}\{\lambda_{\min}(\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}\Sigma_{e})\}\geq\min_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}/(c_{1}\kappa)$ , there exists some non-random large enough $p_{0}$ s.t. $\forall\,p\geq p_{0}$ , $\min_{S\subset[p],e\in[E]}\{\lambda_{\min}(\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S})\}\geq\min_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}/(2c_{1}\kappa)$ . For $p\geq p_{0}$ , we can invoke Lemma F.6 to get $\mathbb{P}[\sigma_{\min}\left((X_{\mathrm{stack}})_{\cdot,S}\right)\leq c]\leq\mathbb{P}[(\min_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}/(2c_{1}\kappa))^{1/2}\sigma_{\min}((X_{\mathrm{temp}})_{\cdot,S})\leq c],\ \forall\,c>0$ . When we think about all the possible index sets $S\subset[p],\lvert S\rvert=k\leq p$ for some $k\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ ,

$$ \mathbb{P}\left[\kappa_{-}(X_{\mathrm{stack}},k)\leq c\right]\leq\binom{p}{k}\mathbb{P}\left[\sigma_{\min}((X_{\mathrm{temp}})_{\cdot,S})\leq\frac{c}{(\min_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}/(2c_{1}\kappa))^{1/2}}\right],\ \forall\,c>0, $$

where we have used a union bound over all possible $S\subset[p],\lvert S\rvert=k$ and the fact that $(X_{\mathrm{temp}})_{\cdot,S}$ has the same marginal distribution for any $S\subset[p],\lvert S\rvert=k$ .

Everything from here follows exactly the same steps as those of Lemma 5, Huang [81] (specifically, after its Equation (63)). With the same proof, we arrive at the following fact: For $k\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ , if $\lim_{N}\frac{k}{N}=\omega\in(0,+\infty)$ , and additionally $\omega\in(0,1)$ only when $\kappa\geq 1$ , then there exists some small constant $c^{\prime}$ and large $p_{0}$ s.t. fixing any small $c\in(0,c^{\prime})$ , the non-asymptotic bound holds $\forall\,p\geq p_{0}$ :

$$ \mathbb{P}\left[\kappa_{-}(X_{\mathrm{stack}},k)\leq c\right]\leq C_{1}\exp\left(-C_{2}\cdot p\right)\quad\text{for some constants }C_{1},C_{2}>0. $$

We argue $\lfloor p(\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon)\rfloor$ qualifies as the choice of ‘ $k$ ’ in the above fact for small enough $\epsilon>0$ . $\lim_{p}p(\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon)/N=\kappa\,(\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon)$ . Assumption 4(a) implies $\overline{\delta}_{e}<\kappa_{e}^{-1}$ , so $\kappa\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}<1$ . We can make $\epsilon$ small enough s.t. $\kappa(\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon)$ is strictly smaller than one when it is needed for $\kappa\geq 1$ . The proof is then complete after taking $p\to\infty$ . ∎

We are finally ready to prove Lemma C.6.

#### Proof of Lemma C.6.

We still assume without loss of generality that $\pi_{e}>0$ for all $e\in[E]$ . Recall the loss function defined in Equation (2) and re-expressed as $L(b)=\frac{1}{2}\lVert y_{\mathrm{stack}}-X_{\mathrm{stack}}\beta\rVert_{2}^{2}+\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda})b\rVert_{1}$ . Define $\Delta\eta^{t}=\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}-\eta^{t}$ . Since $\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}$ minimizes the loss, $L(\eta^{t}+\Delta\eta^{t})\leq L(\eta^{t})$ .

Applying Lemma F.6(b) and then Lemma F.4(a) to $X_{\mathrm{stack}}$ defined in Equation (C-21), we know $\sigma_{\max}(X_{\mathrm{stack}})\leq 2(\max_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}c_{1}/\kappa)^{1/2}(1+\sqrt{\kappa})$ holds almost surely as $p\to\infty$ .

We now define the high-probability event we will be working on throughout the proof. We choose $\epsilon_{0}\in(0,1)$ small enough and $M>1$ large enough s.t. $\forall\,\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_{0})$ , $\exists\,T$ s.t. $\forall\,t\geq T$ , at the time step $t$ , the following conditions are satisfied simultaneously with probability going to 1 as $p\to\infty$ :

- (i) $\max\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2},\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\eta^{t}\rVert_{2},\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\vec{\lambda}\rVert_{2}\}\leq M$ (by Lemma C.1, Lemma C.2 and Assumption 3(a));

- (ii) $\lvert S^{t}(c_{2})\rvert\leq p(\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}+{\epsilon})$ for some $c_{2}=c_{2}(\epsilon)\in(0,1)$ (by Lemma C.5 with $c_{2}$ depending on the specific $\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_{0})$ but invariant to the choice of the time step $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ );

- (iii) $\kappa_{-}(X_{\mathrm{stack}},p(\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+2{\epsilon}))>c_{3}$ for some $c_{3}=c_{3}(\epsilon_{0})\in(0,1)$ (by Lemma C.10 with $c_{3}$ depending on the upper bound $\epsilon_{0}$ );

- (iv) $\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\nabla L(\eta^{t})\rVert_{2}<\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/(2M^{2})$ (by Lemma C.4; the only condition that determines the choice of $T$ );

- (v) $\sigma_{\max}(X_{\mathrm{stack}})\leq c_{4}=2(\max_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}c_{1}/\kappa)^{1/2}(1+\sqrt{\kappa})$ .

In particular, the use of Lemma C.10 in condition (iii) has also required $\kappa\,(\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+2{\epsilon_{0}})<1$ which will be needed later. We also let $c_{5}>0$ be a value that satisfies $\liminf_{p}\min_{j\in[p]}\{\vec{\lambda}_{j}\}>c_{5}$ by Assumption 3(a).

Let $S=\mathrm{supp}(\eta^{t})\subset[p]$ . Recall $s^{t}$ defined in Equation (C-14) from Lemma C.4 is a sub-gradient of $\lVert\eta^{t}\rVert_{1}$ , and $\nabla L(\eta^{t})$ in Lemma C.4 is defined using $s^{t}$ . We have the following inequalities:

$$ \displaystyle 0\geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\left[L(\eta^{t}+\Delta\eta^{t})-L(\eta^{t})\right] \displaystyle\geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\left(\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S})(\eta^{t}_{S}+\Delta\eta^{t}_{S})\rVert_{1}-\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S})\eta^{t}_{S}\rVert_{1}\right)+\frac{1}{p}\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})\Delta\eta^{t}_{S^{c}}\rVert_{1}+\frac{1}{2p}\lVert X_{\mathrm{stack}}\Delta\eta^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2} \displaystyle-\frac{1}{p}(y_{\mathrm{stack}}-X_{\mathrm{stack}}\eta^{t})^{{\top}}X_{\mathrm{stack}}\Delta\eta^{t} \displaystyle\geq \displaystyle\underbrace{\frac{1}{p}\left(\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S})(\eta^{t}_{S}+\Delta\eta^{t}_{S})\rVert_{1}-\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S})\eta^{t}_{S}\rVert_{1}-\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S})\mathop{\mathrm{sign}}(\eta^{t}_{S})^{{\top}}\Delta\eta^{t}_{S}\right)}_{(1)} \displaystyle+\underbrace{\frac{1}{p}\left(\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})\Delta\eta^{t}_{S^{c}}\rVert_{1}-[\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})s^{t}_{S^{c}}]^{{}^{{\top}}}\Delta\eta^{t}_{S^{c}}\right)}_{(2)}+\underbrace{\frac{1}{2p}\lVert X_{\mathrm{stack}}\Delta\eta^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}}_{(3)} \displaystyle+\frac{1}{p}(\nabla L(\eta^{t}))^{{\top}}\Delta\eta^{t}. $$

The terms $(1)$ , $(2)$ and $(3)$ are all non-negative. In particular for $(1)$ , we can use the following inequality for any two real numbers $a,b$ : $\lvert a+b\rvert\geq\lvert a\rvert+b\cdot\mathop{\mathrm{sign}}(a)$ . Since the terms $(1)$ , $(2)$ and $(3)$ are all non-negative, we must have $(\nabla L(\eta^{t}))^{{\top}}\Delta\eta^{t}\leq 0$ . By conditions (i), (iv) of the high-probability event and Cauchy’s inequality, we know

$$ \lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[(1)+(2)+(3)\leq\frac{1}{p}\lvert(\nabla L(\eta^{t}))^{{\top}}\Delta\eta^{t}\rvert\leq\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/M\right]=1. $$

Respectively for terms (2) and (3), the above tells us on the high probability event,

$$ \displaystyle 0\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})\Delta\eta^{t}_{S^{c}}\rVert_{1}-\frac{1}{p}[\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})s^{t}_{S^{c}}]^{{\top}}\Delta\eta^{t}_{S^{c}}\leq\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/M, \displaystyle 0\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert X_{\mathrm{stack}}\Delta\eta^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 2\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/M. $$

Take the SVD of $X_{\mathrm{stack}}:\,X_{\mathrm{stack}}=\sum_{i=1}^{N\land p}\sigma_{i}u_{i}v_{i}^{{\top}}$ , assuming $\sigma_{1}\geq\sigma_{2}\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_{N\land p}$ . Let $V_{(1)}=\Span(v_{i}:\sigma_{i}\geq c_{3}/2)$ and $V_{(2)}$ be the orthogonal complement of $V_{(1)}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{p}$ . Let $P_{(1)},P_{(2)}$ be the projection matrices of $V_{(1)}$ and $V_{(2)}$ . Denote $X_{(1)}=X_{\mathrm{stack}}P_{(1)}$ and $X_{(1)}=X_{\mathrm{stack}}P_{(2)}$ . Then $X_{(1)}^{{\top}}X_{(2)}=0$ . Define $\Delta\eta_{(1)}=P_{(1)}\Delta\eta^{t}$ , $\Delta\eta_{(2)}=P_{(2)}\Delta\eta^{t}$ . The second line of Equation (C-23) implies

$$ \frac{1}{p}\lVert X_{(1)}\Delta\eta_{(1)}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 2\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/M,\quad\frac{1}{p}\lVert X_{(2)}\Delta\eta_{(2)}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 2\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/M. $$

For $\Delta\eta_{(1)}$ corresponding to the larger singular values, we consequently have

$$ \frac{1}{p}\lVert\Delta\eta_{(1)}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 8\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/(c_{3}^{2})\leq 8\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{2}/M, $$

and we are left to bound $\frac{1}{p}\lVert\Delta\eta_{(2)}\rVert_{2}^{2}$ .

We use the first line of Equation (C-23) to bound $\frac{1}{p}\lVert\Delta\eta_{(2)}\rVert_{2}^{2}$ . For $\Delta\eta_{(1)}$ , we have

$$ \frac{1}{p}[\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})s^{t}_{S^{c}}]^{{\top}}(\Delta\eta_{(1)})_{S^{c}}\leq\frac{1}{p}\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})(\Delta\eta_{(1)})_{S^{c}}\rVert_{1}\leq\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}}\rVert\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\Delta\hat{\beta}_{(1)}\rVert_{2}\leq 2\sqrt{2}\epsilon c_{2}c_{3}, $$

where we have used Cauchy’s inequality and the bound on $\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\vec{\lambda}\rVert_{2}$ from (i) of the high-probability event. Since $\Delta\eta_{(2)}=\Delta\eta^{t}-\Delta\eta_{(1)}$ , we know

$$ \frac{1}{p}\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{c}}\rVert_{1}-\frac{1}{p}[\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})s^{t}_{S^{c}}]^{{\top}}(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{c}}\leq\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}+4\sqrt{2}\epsilon c_{2}c_{3}, $$

where we have used the fact that $M>1$ from (i). Recall that for $S^{t}(c_{2})$ defined in Lemma C.5, $S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}\subset S^{c}$ . Hence,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}})(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}}\rVert_{1}-\frac{1}{p}[\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}})s^{t}_{S^{c}}]^{{\top}}(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}}\leq \displaystyle\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}+4\sqrt{2}\epsilon c_{2}c_{3} \displaystyle\iff\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}}\vec{\lambda}_{j}\left[\left\lvert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{j}\right\rvert-s^{t}_{j}(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{j}\right]\leq \displaystyle\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}+4\sqrt{2}\epsilon c_{2}c_{3}. $$

By the definition of $S^{t}(c_{2})$ , $\forall\,j\in S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}$ , $\lvert s^{t}_{j}\rvert<1-c_{2}$ . Also recall we have defined $c_{5}$ to be a constant s.t. $\liminf_{p}\min_{j\in[p]}\{\vec{\lambda}_{j}\}>c_{5}$ . As a result,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}}\rVert_{1}\leq\frac{1}{c_{2}c_{5}}\left(\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/M+4\sqrt{2}\epsilon c_{2}c_{3}\right)\leq(1+4\sqrt{2})\epsilon c_{3}/c_{5}. $$

Recall we have chosen $\kappa\,(\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}+2{\epsilon})<1$ as required by Lemma C.10 used for condition (iii) of the high-probability event. Condition (ii) guarantees $\lvert S^{t}(c_{2})\rvert\leq p(\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}+{\epsilon})$ . Then we immediately know $\lvert S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}\rvert>p{\epsilon}$ , because otherwise $p=\lvert S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}\rvert+\lvert S^{t}(c_{2})\rvert\leq p(\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}+2{\epsilon})<p$ would give a contradiction. We partition $S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}$ disjointly into $S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}=\cup_{l=1}^{K}S_{l}$ , with each $S_{l}$ satisfying $\lvert S_{l}\rvert\in[p{\epsilon}/2,p{\epsilon}]$ , and they are constructed in a descending order in the sense that for any $i\in S_{l}$ and $j\in S_{l+1}$ , $\lvert({\Delta}\eta_{(2)})_{i}\rvert\geq\lvert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{j}\rvert$ . By the disjoint partition,

$$ \frac{1}{p}\lVert\Delta\eta_{(2)}\rVert_{2}^{2}=\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert\left(\Delta\eta_{(2)}\right)_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}+\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert\left(\Delta\eta_{(2)}\right)_{S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}. $$

We bound the two terms on the RHS respectively. For the first term,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert\left(\Delta\eta_{(2)}\right)_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\sum_{l=2}^{K}\left\lVert\left(\Delta\eta_{(2)}\right)_{S_{l}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\frac{1}{p}\sum_{l=2}^{K}\lvert S_{l}\rvert\cdot\left(\frac{\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S_{l-1}}\rVert_{1}}{\lvert S_{l-1}\rvert}\right)^{2} \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\cdot\frac{4}{p\epsilon}\sum_{l=2}^{K}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S_{l-1}}\rVert_{1}^{2}\leq\frac{1}{p}\cdot\frac{4}{p{\epsilon}}\left[\sum_{l=2}^{K}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S_{l-1}}\rVert_{1}\right]^{2} \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{4}{p^{2}{\epsilon}}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}}\rVert_{1}^{2}\leq 4\epsilon c_{3}^{2}(1+4\sqrt{2})^{2}/c_{5}^{2}, $$

where the first inequality is because $\forall\,i\in S_{l}$ , $\lvert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{i}\rvert^{2}\leq({\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S_{l-1}}\rVert_{1}}/{\lvert S_{l-1}\rvert})^{2}$ ; the second inequality is because $\lvert S_{l}\rvert\in[p{\epsilon}/2,p{\epsilon}]$ for all $l\in[K]$ ; the last inequality is by Equation (C-25).

For the second term, we apply conditions (iii), (v) of the high-probability event:

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{pc_{3}^{2}}\left\lVert(X_{\mathrm{stack}})_{\cdot,S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2} \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{2}{pc_{3}^{2}}\left[\left\lVert X_{\mathrm{stack}}\Delta\eta_{(2)}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}+\left\lVert(X_{\mathrm{stack}})_{\cdot,\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{{}_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{2}{pc_{3}^{2}}\left[\frac{c_{3}^{2}}{4}\left(\left\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}+\left\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right)+c_{4}^{2}\,\left\lVert\left(\Delta\eta_{(2)}\right)_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{2p}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}\rVert_{2}^{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2c_{4}^{2}}{c_{3}^{2}}\right)\frac{1}{p}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}\rVert_{2}^{2}, $$

where the first inequality has used condition (iii); the second inequality is by the triangle inequality; the terms involving ‘ $c_{3}$ ’ after the third inequality is because $\Delta\eta_{(2)}$ is $\Delta\eta^{t}$ projected onto $V_{(2)}$ corresponding to the smaller or null singular values of $X_{\mathrm{stack}}$ . Further, we plug in the bound from Equation (C-26),

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq \displaystyle\left(1+\frac{4c_{4}^{2}}{c_{3}^{2}}\right)\frac{1}{p}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 4\epsilon\left(c_{3}^{2}+4c_{4}^{2}\right)(1+4\sqrt{2})^{2}/c_{5}^{2}, $$

which, put together with Equation (C-26) and Equation (C-24), yields

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert\Delta\eta_{(2)}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 8\epsilon\left(c_{3}^{2}+2c_{4}^{2}\right)(1+4\sqrt{2})^{2}/c_{5}^{2} \displaystyle\implies \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert\Delta\eta^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\left[{8}\epsilon c_{2}^{2}{c_{3}^{2}}+8\left(c_{3}^{2}+2c_{4}^{2}\right)(1+4\sqrt{2})^{2}/c_{5}^{2}\right]\cdot{\epsilon}\leq\left[{8}+8\left(1+2c_{4}^{2}\right)(1+4\sqrt{2})^{2}/c_{5}^{2}\right]\cdot{\epsilon}. $$

Recall that $c_{4}=2(\max_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}c_{1}/\kappa)^{1/2}(1+\sqrt{\kappa})$ , $c_{5}<\liminf_{p}\min_{j\in[p]}\{\vec{\lambda}_{j}\}$ . Both are fixed constants free of $\epsilon$ or $p$ , $t$ . This completes the proof of Lemma C.6. To re-iterate what we have proved: There exists some small $\epsilon_{0}\in(0,1)$ , s.t. $\forall\,\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_{0})$ , $\exists\,T$ s.t. $\forall\,t\geq T$ , $\lim_{p}\mathbb{P}\left[\frac{1}{p}\lVert\eta^{t}-\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}<\epsilon\right]=1$ . ∎

## Appendix D Proof of Theorem 3

For each environment $e\in[E]$ , $\hat{\beta}_{e}$ defined in Equation (9) is a special case of the stacked Lasso $\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}$ , because if we set ‘ $E=1$ ’ in the stacked Lasso, we naturally get the Lasso estimator fit on a single environment. This allows us to use the tools already prepared for the stacked Lasso to study every individual estimator $\hat{\beta}_{e}$ , $e\in[E]$ .

Specially for the GLAMP part, we let ‘ $E=1$ ’ and get the special cases of Definitions C.1 and C.2 as the following Definitions D.1 and D.2:

#### Definition D.1 (Multi-Environment GLAMP Formulation).

Under Assumptions 2,5,6 (a), we define AMP iterates for each environment as below:

$$ \displaystyle v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}= \displaystyle{\displaystyle X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}(y_{e}-r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t-1})-\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}+\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\eta_{e}(v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t-1}), \displaystyle r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}= \displaystyle{\displaystyle X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\eta_{e}(v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t})-\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{\mathrm{ind},e}(y_{e}-r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t-1}) $$

for all $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ and $e\in[E]$ . In Equation (D-27), $\overline{\delta}_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{(p)}=\frac{1}{\tau_{\mathrm{ind},e}p}\mathbb{E}\left[Z_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\overline{\eta}_{e}(\tau_{e})\right]$ has been in Proposition 2 and specified with $\tau_{\mathrm{ind},e}=\tau_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{*}\,\forall\,e\in[E]$ and $\theta_{e}=\theta_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{*}$ .

As initialization, we define $\eta_{e}^{0}$ as follows: Let $Z_{e}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,(\tau_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{*})^{2}I_{p}),\,\forall\,e\in[E]$ be independent Gaussian variables, and they are also independent of $\{{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}:e\in[E]\}$ ; define $\eta_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{0}=\eta_{e}(Z_{e}),\,\forall\,e\in[E]$ . We initialize $r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{0}={X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\eta_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{0}$ , $v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{1}={X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}(y_{e}-r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{0})-\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}+\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\eta_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{0}$ , $\forall\,e\in[E]$ .

As a shorthand, define $\eta_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}=\eta_{e}(v_{e}^{t})$ for $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ .

#### Definition D.2 (State Evolution).

Let $\{\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},V,e)}:e\in[E]\}$ be $E$ infinite dimensional matrices. They are defined separately without using each other. $\forall\,e\in[E]$ ,

For all $i\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ , $(\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},V,e)})_{i,i}=(\tau_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{*})^{2}$ .

For all $i<j$ , $i,j\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ , $(\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},V,e)})_{i,j}=(\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},V,e)})_{j,i}=(\tau_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{*})^{2}\rho_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{i,j}$ , where $\rho_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{i,j}\in[0,1]$ . For the definition of $\{\rho^{i,j}_{\mathrm{ind},e}\}$ : (i) For all $j\geq 2$ , $\rho^{1,j}_{\mathrm{ind},e}=H_{\mathrm{ind},e}(0)$ ; (ii) For all $2\leq i<j$ , $\rho_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{i,j}=H_{\mathrm{ind},e}(\rho_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{i-1,j-1})$ . $H_{\mathrm{ind},e}$ has been defined in Assumption 6 (b).

In particular, we define the $t$ -dimensional top-left block of $\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},V,e)}$ as $\Sigma^{t}_{(\mathrm{ind},V,e)}=(\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},V,e)})_{[t],[t]}$ , $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ .

Definitions D.1 and D.2 are just the GLAMP formulation for the stacked Lasso applied to each individual environment and put together. As a corollary of Lemma C.6, we already know $\eta_{e}(v^{t}_{\mathrm{ind},e})$ converges to $\hat{\beta}_{e}$ in the sense that

$$ \forall\,\epsilon>0,\ \exists\,T,s.t.\forall\,t\geq T,\ \lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert\eta_{e}(v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t})-\hat{\beta}_{e}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}<\epsilon\right]=1. $$

However, results of the stacked Lasso applied to each $\hat{\beta}_{e}$ only gives us the asymptotic behavior within one environment. In other words, Theorem 2 only implies for a single environment that $\left\lvert\phi(\overline{\eta}_{e},\beta_{e})-\phi(\hat{\beta}_{e},\beta_{e})\right\rvert=o_{\mathsf{P}}(1)$ for any pseudo-Lipschitz function $\phi$ . But this is not enough for the proof of Theorem 3, which is the joint convergence of all the environments. It turns out that the GLAMP iterates in Definition D.1 can also be cast in a multi-environment GLAMP instance, which gives us the desired joint convergence of all environments. This is shown by Lemma D.1:

#### Lemma D.1 (GLAMP Convergence).

Under Assumptions 2,5,6, and Definitions D.1,D.2, $\forall\,t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ , $\forall\,$ sequence of order- $k$ pseudo-Lipschitz functions $\phi:(\mathbb{R}^{p})^{(t+2)E}\to\mathbb{R}$ , $k\geq 1$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\phi\left(v_{\mathrm{ind},1}^{t},\cdots,v_{\mathrm{ind},E}^{t},v_{\mathrm{ind},1}^{t-1},\cdots,v_{\mathrm{ind},E}^{t-1},\cdots,v_{\mathrm{ind},1}^{1},\cdots,v_{\mathrm{ind},E}^{1},\eta^{0}_{1},\cdots,\eta^{0}_{E},\beta_{1},\beta_{2},\cdots,\beta_{E}\right) \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\phi\left(Z^{t}_{1},\cdots,Z^{t}_{E},Z^{t-1}_{1},\cdots,Z^{t-1}_{E},\cdots,Z^{1}_{1},\cdots,Z^{1}_{E},\eta_{1}(Z_{1}^{0}),\cdots,\eta_{E}(Z_{E}^{0}),\beta_{1},\beta_{2},\cdots,\beta_{E}\right)\right]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1). $$

In the expectation on the RHS, we have (i) $\{Z_{e}^{i}:e\in[E],0\leq i\leq t\}$ are jointly Gaussian; (ii) $\{Z_{e}^{0}:e\in[E]\}\mathchoice{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\displaystyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\displaystyle\perp}}}{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\textstyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\textstyle\perp}}}{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\scriptstyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\scriptstyle\perp}}}{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\scriptscriptstyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle\perp}}}\{Z_{e}^{i}:e\in[E],i\geq 1\}$ and $\{Z_{e}^{0}:e\in[E]\}$ follows the distribution described in Definition D.2; (iii) For the other Gaussian vectors, the matrices $[Z_{e}^{1}|Z_{e}^{2}|\cdots|Z_{e}^{t}]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times t}$ has iid rows drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},V,e)}^{t})$ , and the $E$ matrices are mutually independent.

Lemma D.1 is proved in Section D.1. Now we are ready to prove Theorem 3.

#### Proof of Theorem 3.

Applying Lemma C.1 to each $\hat{\beta}_{e}$ , we know $\exists\,M$ s.t. $\sup_{e}\limsup_{p}\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{e}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq M$ a.s.. Combined with Equation (D-28), we can choose $M$ large enough, s.t. for any order- $k$ pseudo-Lipschitz function $\phi:\mathbb{R}^{2E}\to\mathbb{R}$ , $k\geq 1$ , $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , $\exists\,T$ s.t. for $t\geq T$ ,

$$ \displaystyle \displaystyle\left\lvert\phi\left(\eta_{1}(v^{t}_{\mathrm{ind},1}),\cdots,\eta_{E}(v^{t}_{\mathrm{ind},E}),\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E}\right)-\phi(\hat{\beta}_{1},\cdots,\hat{\beta}_{E},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})\right\rvert \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle L\sum_{e\in[E]}\left[1+\left(\frac{\lVert\beta_{e}\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}}\right)^{k-1}+\left(\frac{\lVert\eta_{e}^{t}(v^{t}_{\mathrm{ind},e})\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}}\right)^{k-1}+\left(\frac{\lVert\hat{\beta}_{e}\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}}\right)^{k-1}\right]\sum_{e\in[E]}\frac{\lVert\eta_{e}(v^{t}_{\mathrm{ind},e})-\hat{\beta}_{e}\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}} \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle 3L\cdot E\cdot M^{(k-1)/2}\sum_{e\in[E]}\frac{\lVert\eta_{e}(v^{t}_{\mathrm{ind},e})-\hat{\beta}_{e}\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}}\leq\epsilon $$

holds with probability approaching one as $p\to\infty$ .

For the same $\epsilon$ and $t$ , Lemma D.1 implies

$$ \left\lvert\phi\left(\eta_{1}(v^{t}_{\mathrm{ind},1}),\cdots,\eta_{e}(v^{t}_{\mathrm{ind},E}),\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E}\right)-\mathbb{E}\left[\phi(\overline{\eta}_{1},\cdots,\overline{\eta}_{E},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})\right]\right\rvert\leq\epsilon $$

with probability approaching one as $p\to\infty$ . Combining the above line with Equation (D-29) proves Theorem 3. ∎

### D.1 Proof of Lemma D.1

#### Proof of Lemma D.1.

Just like the proof of Lemma C.2, we specify a multi-environment GLAMP instance that has the form and state evolution as described in Definitions D.1 and D.2. Also analogously to the proof of Lemma C.2, we can use a sub-sequence based argument to address the technicality caused by using random initialization in the GLAMP instance. We then move on to describe the instance itself.

Same as the GLAMP instance for the stack Lasso estimator, let $\{q_{e}:e\in[E]\}$ all be sufficiently large and fixed integers, let $B=[\beta_{1}|\beta_{2}|\cdots|\beta_{E}|\eta^{0}|0|0|\cdots]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}$ , and $W_{e}=[w_{e}|0|0|\cdots]\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{e}\times q}$ . Now we have verified the GLAMP iterates take the form of Definition D.1 and their state evolution is described by Definition D.2. By GLAMP convergence, we have shown Lemma D.1. ∎

The proof follows the exact same steps as those of our Lemma C.1, or Lemma 3.2 of Bayati and Montanari [32], so we only point out some key steps this time. $$ v_{e}^{\infty}=\frac{{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}(y_{e}-{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})}{1-\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}}+\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}-\beta_{e}),\quad r_{e}^{\infty}=y_{e}-\frac{y_{e}-{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}}{1-\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}}. $$

#### Lemma E.10.

Fixing $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ , for any sequence of order- $k$ pseudo-Lipschitz functions $\phi:(\mathbb{R}^{p})^{(t+1)\times(E+1)+E}\to\mathbb{R}$ , $k\geq 1$ , define

where the Gaussian variables on the right hand side are exactly from the limit in Lemma E.2. We define another quantity $B$ :

Then we have

$$ \lim_{t_{0}\to\infty}\sup_{p\geq 1}\left\lvert E[A]-E[B]\right\rvert=0. $$

#### Proof of Lemma E.10.

If we write the Gaussian variables used by $A$ and $B$ into matrices $Z_{A},Z_{B}\in\mathbb{R}^{(p\times(t+1)(E+1))}$ :

$$ \displaystyle Z_{A}= \displaystyle[Z_{\textup{II}}^{t}|Z_{\textup{II}}^{t-1}|\cdots|Z_{\textup{II}}^{1}|Z_{\textup{II}}^{0}|Z^{t+t_{0}}_{1}|\cdots|Z^{t+t_{0}}_{E}|Z^{t+t_{0}-1}_{1}|\cdots|Z^{t+t_{0}-1}_{E}|\cdots|Z^{t_{0}}_{1}|\cdots|Z^{t_{0}}_{E}], \displaystyle Z_{B}= \displaystyle[Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t}|Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t-1}|\cdots|Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{1}|Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{0}|Z_{1}|\cdots|Z_{E}|Z_{1}|\cdots|Z_{E}|\cdots|Z_{1}|\cdots|Z_{E}]. $$

Then by the definitions of the Gaussian variables from Lemma E.2 and Lemma E.10, we know both $Z_{A}$ and $Z_{B}$ have iid rows drawn from some $(t+1)(E+1)$ -dimensional Gaussian distribution, with mean zero and covariance matrices $\Sigma_{A}$ and $\Sigma_{B}$ . Both covariance matrices are $(t+1)(E+1)$ -dimensional and do not depend on $p$ .

We first show $\lim_{t_{0}\to\infty}\lVert\Sigma_{A}-\Sigma_{B}\rVert_{2}=0$ .

By definition, $\Sigma_{B}\in\mathbb{R}^{(t+1)(E+1)\times(t+1)(E+1)}$ do not depend on $t_{0}$ . On the other hand for $\Sigma_{A}$ , by Lemma C.3, $\lim_{t_{0}\to\infty}\sup_{j>i\geq 0,e\in[E]}\rho^{t_{0}+i,t_{0}+j}_{e}=1$ . Hence for any fixed $e\in[E]$ , if we look at the marginal distribution of each row of $[Z_{e}^{t+t_{0}}|Z_{e}^{t+t_{0}-1}|\cdots|Z_{e}^{t_{0}}]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times(t+1)}$ , all the $(t+1)$ elements become perfectly correlated as $t_{0}\to\infty$ ; in other words, the elements in $\Sigma_{A}$ corresponding to their covariances converge to $(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}$ . Among different environments, we know for different $e\in[E]$ , $\{[Z_{e}^{t+t_{0}}|Z_{e}^{t+t_{0}-1}|\cdots|Z_{e}^{t_{0}}]:e\in[E]\}$ are independent Gaussian matrices. As a result, we have proved that for the lower-right sub-blocks:

$$ \lim_{t_{0}\to\infty}(\Sigma_{A})_{(t+2):(t+1)(E+1),\,(t+2):(t+1)(E+1)}=(\Sigma_{B})_{(t+2):(t+1)(E+1),\,(t+2):(t+1)(E+1)}. $$

For the first $(t+1)$ rows of $Z_{A}$ , we know from Lemma E.2 that $Z_{\textup{II}}^{i}=\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\zeta^{*}Z_{1}^{t_{0}+i}/\tau_{1}^{*}+\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}}(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{i}$ for some $(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{i}\mathchoice{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\displaystyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\displaystyle\perp}}}{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\textstyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\textstyle\perp}}}{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\scriptstyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\scriptstyle\perp}}}{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\scriptscriptstyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle\perp}}}Z_{1}^{t_{0}+i}$ , $\forall\,0\leq i\leq t$ . For convenience, we apply a linear transformation to $Z_{A}$ , take an excerpt at two time steps $0\leq i<j\leq t$ , and consider the Gaussian matrix $[\frac{1}{\tau_{1}^{*}}Z_{1}^{i+t_{0}}|(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{i}|\frac{1}{\tau_{2}^{*}}Z_{2}^{i+t_{0}}|\cdots|\frac{1}{\tau_{E}^{*}}Z_{E}^{i+t_{0}}|\frac{1}{\tau_{1}^{*}}Z_{1}^{j+t_{0}}|(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{j}|\frac{1}{\tau_{2}^{*}}Z_{2}^{j+t_{0}}|\cdots|\frac{1}{\tau_{E}^{*}}Z_{E}^{j+t_{0}}]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times 2(E+1)}$ . Each row of it follows a $2(E+1)$ -dimensional Gaussian distribution, which we denote as $\mathcal{G}^{i,j}$ .

We focus on the correlation between the two elements in each iid row of $[(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{i}|(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{j}]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times 2}$ , which we denote as $\varrho^{i,j}$ . We want to show $\lim_{t_{0}to\infty}\varrho^{i,j}=(\Sigma_{(V,\textup{II})})_{i,j}$ , and then the upper-left block of $\Sigma_{A}$ will also converge to that of $\Sigma_{B}$ . This is because for columns of $B$ , $Z_{\textup{II}}^{i}=\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\zeta^{*}Z_{1}/\tau_{1}^{*}+\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}}Z^{i}_{1,\infty}$ and $[Z^{0}_{1,\infty}|Z^{1}_{1,\infty}|\cdots|Z^{t}_{1,\infty}]$ has iid rows from $N(0,\Sigma_{(V,\textup{II})}^{t})$ by construction.

When $i=0$ , $(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{0}=Z^{\mathrm{init}}_{1}$ is independent from all other variables, so $\varrho^{i,j}=0=(\Sigma_{(V,\textup{II})})_{0,j}$ .

When $i\geq 1$ , $\varrho^{i,j}=H_{\textup{II}}^{\epsilon_{H}}(\mathcal{G}^{i-1.j-1})$ . This is because of the GLAMP convergence in Lemma E.2. Then for any $j$ , we can show by induction that $\lim_{t_{0}}\varrho^{i,j}=\lim_{t_{0}\to\infty}H_{\textup{II}}^{\epsilon_{H}}(\mathcal{G}^{i-1.j-1})=H_{\textup{II}}^{\epsilon_{H}}(\lim_{t_{0}}\varrho^{i-1,j-1})$ , and $\lim_{t_{0}}\varrho^{i,j}=(\Sigma_{(V,\textup{II})})_{i,j}$ .

As a result, we have proved that for the upper-left sub-blocks:

$$ \lim_{t_{0}\to\infty}(\Sigma_{A})_{[t+1],[t+1]}=(\Sigma_{B})_{[t+1],[t+1]}. $$

For the rest of the elements in $\Sigma_{A}$ , note that the columns of $[Z_{e}^{t+t_{0}}|Z_{e}^{t+t_{0}-1}|\cdots|Z_{e}^{t_{0}}]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times(t+1)}$ becomes perfectly correlated as $t_{0}\to\infty$ , so those elements also converge to the corresponding elements in $\Sigma_{B}$

Thus we have shown $\lim_{t_{0}}\lVert\Sigma_{A}-\Sigma_{B}\rVert_{2}=0$ . From here, following the same argument as Equation (156)-(166) of the proof of Lemma 10, Berthier et al. [41], we arrive at

$$ \lvert\mathbb{E}[A]-\mathbb{E}[B]\rvert^{2}\leq\mathit{Constant}\cdot\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(\Sigma_{A}+\Sigma_{B}-2(\Sigma_{B}^{1/2}\Sigma_{A}\Sigma_{B}^{1/2})^{1/2})=o(\lVert\Sigma_{A}-\Sigma_{B}\rVert_{2}), $$

where the $\mathit{Constant}$ does not depend on $p,t_{0},\Sigma_{A},\Sigma_{B}$ . This completes the proof of Lemma E.10. ∎

Now we are ready to show Lemma E.3.

#### Proof of Lemma E.3.

We first prove by induction on $t$ that $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , $\exists\,T_{0}$ s.t. $\forall\,t_{0}\geq T_{0}$ ,

$$ \lim_{p}\mathbb{P}\left[\frac{1}{p}\lVert v_{\textup{II}}^{t}-v_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\epsilon\right]=1. $$

When $t=0$ , $v_{\textup{II}}^{0}=\zeta^{*}\cdot\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}v_{1}^{t_{0}}/\tau_{1}^{*}+\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}}\cdot\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}Z_{\textup{II}}^{\mathrm{init}}$ , $v_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{0}=\zeta^{*}\cdot\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}v_{1}^{\infty}/\tau_{1}^{*}+\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}}\cdot\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}Z_{\textup{II}}^{\mathrm{init}}$ . Then Equation (E-34) directly follows from Lemma E.9. Now suppose we have proved Equation (E-34) for all $0\leq i\leq t-1$ . For $t$ ,

$$ \displaystyle v_{\textup{II}}^{t}= \displaystyle{\displaystyle X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}(y_{1}-r_{\textup{II}}^{t-1}-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}(y_{1}-r_{1}^{t+t_{0}-1}))-(1-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}^{(p)}_{\textup{I}})\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\beta_{1}-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}^{(p)}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\eta^{t+t_{0}-1} \displaystyle+\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\xi(v_{\textup{II}}^{t-1},\eta^{t+t_{0}-1}), \displaystyle v_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t}= \displaystyle{\displaystyle X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}(y_{1}-r_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t-1}-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}(y_{1}-r_{1}^{\infty}))-(1-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}^{(p)}_{\textup{I}})\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\beta_{1}-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}^{(p)}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}} \displaystyle+\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\xi(v_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t-1},\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}), $$

and Equation (E-34) follows from Lemma E.9 and the induction hypothesis.

We know from Lemma E.2 that

$$ \displaystyle\phi\left(v_{\textup{II}}^{t},v_{\textup{II}}^{t-1},\cdots,v_{\textup{II}}^{1},v_{\textup{II}}^{0},v_{1}^{t+t_{0}},\eta^{t+t_{0}},\beta_{1},\beta_{2},\cdots,\beta_{E}\right)+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1) \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\phi\left(Z_{\textup{II}}^{t},Z_{\textup{II}}^{t-1},\cdots,Z_{\textup{II}}^{1},Z_{\textup{II}}^{0},Z^{t+t_{0}}_{1},\eta(Z_{1}^{t+t_{0}},\cdots,Z_{E}^{t+t_{0}}),\beta_{1},\beta_{2},\cdots,\beta_{E}\right)\right]. $$

We wish to take $t_{0}\to\infty$ on both sides of Equation (E-35) to prove Lemma E.3.

For the LHS of Equation (E-35), by Equation (E-34) and Lemma E.9, $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , $\exists\,T_{0}$ s.t. $\forall\,t_{0}\geq T_{0}$ and $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ ,

where the Gaussian variables are as they are defined in Lemma E.2.

For the RHS of Equation (E-35), by Lemma E.10, $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , $\exists\,T_{0}$ s.t. $\forall\,t_{0}\geq T_{0}$ and $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\sup_{p}\Big|\mathbb{E}\left[\phi\left(Z_{\textup{II}}^{t},Z_{\textup{II}}^{t-1},\cdots,Z_{\textup{II}}^{1},Z_{\textup{II}}^{0},Z^{t+t_{0}}_{1},\eta(Z_{1}^{t+t_{0}},\cdots,Z_{1}^{t+t_{0}}),\beta_{1},\beta_{2},\cdots,\beta_{E}\right)\right] \displaystyle-\mathbb{E}\left[\phi\left(Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t},Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t-1},\cdots,Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{1},Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{0},Z_{1},\overline{\eta},\beta_{1},\beta_{2},\cdots,\beta_{E}\right)\right]\Big|<\epsilon, $$

where the Gaussian variables are as they are defined in the term ‘ $B$ ’ in Lemma E.10.

Putting the analysis of both sides together, we know

$$ \displaystyle\phi\left(v_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t},v_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t-1},\cdots,v_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{1},v_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{0},v_{1}^{\infty},\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}},\beta_{1},\beta_{2},\cdots,\beta_{E}\right)+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1) \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\phi\left(Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t},Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t-1},\cdots,Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{1},Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{0},Z_{1},\overline{\eta},\beta_{1},\beta_{2},\cdots,\beta_{E}\right)\right], $$

which completes the proof of Lemma E.3. ∎

#### E.1.4 Proof of Lemma E.4

Let $\widetilde{H}_{\textup{II}}(\cdot)=(H_{\textup{II}}(\cdot)-(\zeta^{*})^{2})/(1-(\zeta^{*})^{2})$ . By Lemma E.8, $\widetilde{H}_{\textup{II}}(\cdot)$ is increasing, strictly convex, $\widetilde{H}_{\textup{II}}(1)=1$ , $\widetilde{H}_{\textup{II}}(0)\geq 0$ . Also, $0\leq\frac{\mathrm{d}\widetilde{H}_{\textup{II}}(\rho)}{\mathrm{d}\rho}\leq\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}<1$ by the last equation in Assumption 8 (a). By Definition E.3,

#### E.1.5 Proof of Lemma E.5

Either $\mu_{\textup{II}}=\mu_{\mathrm{joint}}$ or $\mu_{\mathrm{ada}}$ , we can use the definition of $\xi$ in Eqn (20) to write out the KKT condition of $\xi^{t}=\xi(v_{\textup{II}}^{t},\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})$ ,

$$ s_{\textup{II}}^{t}=\frac{1}{\theta_{\textup{II}}^{*}}\left[\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}v_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t}+(1-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}})\Sigma_{1}(\beta_{1}-\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})-\Sigma_{1}(\xi^{t}-\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})\right]\in\nabla\mu_{\textup{II}}(\xi^{t};\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}). $$

To show the claim about $\nabla L_{\textup{II}}(\xi^{t})$ , we again use the $o^{*}_{\mathbb{P}}(\sqrt{p})$ notation defined in the proof of Lemma C.4 in Section C.1.4. To recall its definition, some sequence $X^{(p),t}=o^{*}_{\mathbb{P}}(\sqrt{p})$ iff $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , $\exists\,T$ s.t. $\forall\,t\geq T$ , $\lim_{p}\mathbb{P}\left[\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert X^{{(p),t}}\rVert_{2}<\epsilon\right]=1$ .

#### E.1.6 Proof of Lemma E.6

The proof of Lemma E.6 only slightly differs for $\mu_{\textup{II}}=\mu_{\mathrm{joint}}$ and $\mu_{\textup{II}}=\mu_{\mathrm{ada}}$ . We will use the former as an example and the latter can be proved in an analogous way.

We define some re-scaled quantities for the subsequent proof.
